The project proposes substantial alteration of an existing historic resource (Delucchi Sheet Metal Works), a two-story with basement 9,892-square-foot industrial building, to allow construction of a vertical and horizontal six-story residential mixed-use building.

The existing building on the 5,257-sqft subject lot was constructed in 1916/1921 and identified in the North Beach Historic Survey (adopted 1999) as an individually significant historic resource. The proposed building would result in a 6-story building containing 20 residential dwelling units, and  nine vehicular parking spaces.

Using the Individually Requested State Density Bonus, the project is seeking the maximum residential density bonus under California State Density Bonus Law of 50% (or 7 units) to allow for 20 total dwelling units. The proposal requests waivers from the following Planning Code requirements: 

1)Rear Yard (Section 134) 
2)  Dwelling Unit Exposure (Section140); and
3) Height (Section 260); and

The project also seeks an incentive or concession under State Density Bonus Law to the Ground Floor Commercial use requirement (Section 722/780.3) to provide a ground floor residential unit.

The proposed project would convert the existing two-story (above basement) 28,863-square-foot parking garage on the site to office use, including a new elevator, building entrance, and bathroom upgrades. The building was constructed in 1927 and is located within the Northeast Waterfront Historic District. The project would include minor interior and exterior modifications including replacing the ground floor on the first level (removing vehicle ramps and replacing with concrete flooring to match existing floors at grade), replacing the windows on the first level to match the existing second story windows, constructing a new entryway with an awning, and removing two roll-up doors and replacing them with windows and bulkheads to match the existing facade. The project would require approximately 18 cubic yards of soil excavation for the elevator pit. The existing building envelope would remain the same. The project would include 6 class 1 bicycle parking spaces in a storage room as well as two off-street vehicle parking spaces on the basement level. On Sansome Street, two existing curb cuts would be replaced with improved sidewalk. The north-most existing curb cut on Sansome Street would be retained to access the two vehicle parking spaces on the basement level of the building. The project will also include removal of the existing steel windows at the non-visible rear east elevation and installation of new fire-rated metal windows in the slightly modified existing openings.

PROJECT REVISED 1/19/2024
The proposed project would demolish the existing 2-story, 33,069 sf parking garage and construct a new 24-story above grade and 1-story below grade mixed-use structure. The building contains 13,710 sf retail space and 132 dwelling units including 26 on-site BMR units (16 units of 80% AMI and 10 units of 120% AMI). 140 unbundled parking spaces and 2 car share spaces are proposed in a garage accessed from Sansome Street. This project will apply for an individually requested state density bonus program with additional bonus allowed from AB-1287. The project qualifies for the following Planning Code waivers: 1) Height 2) Bulk 3) Open Space, and 4) Rear Yard. The additional density proposed by the modified project is available based on the application of additional density bonus, waivers, and concessions/incentives from AB 1287. The project seeks an incentive/concessions to: 1) Collapse the affordable income tiers and 2) allow garage within the North Beach-Telegraph Hill SUD/ allow a Sansome Street curb cut/ allow parking ration above 0.5 spaces/unit.

The subject property is a through lot fronting Pacific Avenue with its rear frontage along Bernard Street. The project proposes the demolition of the one-story commercial building at 1270 Pacific Avenue and new construction of a four-story, two-unit, residential building. At the north end of the lot, 169 Bernard Street, the project proposes to retain the existing two story, one-family dwelling with a new one-story vertical addition and interior work. Open space would be provided in a centrally located rear yard and at balconies and roof decks. The project would require 43.5 cubic yards of excavation.

The Property is split zoned between the Pacific Avenue NC District and the RH-3 District, with the front of the lot located in the Pacific Avenue NC District. The Project requested a Project Review Meeting (2021-003721PRV) where it was determined that the Pacific Avenue NC District rear yard requirements apply to the entire lot, and a Variance from the RH-3 rear yard requirements would not be necessary. Further, it was established that a Conditional Use authorization under Section 121.1 (development of large lots in NC Districts) would not be required because the portion of the lot actually within the NC District did not meet the size threshold. The proposed project is a 15-story, 100% affordable, senior housing project with 175 units to be built on the combined parcels of 758 and 772 Pacific Avenue in the Chinatown neighborhood. The City and County of San Francisco currently owns the 772 Pacific Avenue parcel and Chinatown Community Development Center ("CCDC"), the nonprofit developer, owns the adjacent 758 Pacific Avenue parcel. The City will acquire the 758 Pacific Avenue parcel from CCDC to merge the two parcels, then ground lease the combined parcel to CCDC to build the senior housing project over the ground floor banquet hall. Modification of a previously approved project - Commission Motion NO. 21055.

The Project includes demolition of the existing commercial parking structure and construction of two, approximately 65-foot-tall, mixed-use buildings that are seven-stories tall on Broadway and eight-stories on Montgomery Street, with approximately 74,515 square feet of residential use and 8,080 square feet of ground floor retail use, including a commercial laundromat. The Project includes 75 dwelling units (11 three-bedroom units, 8 two-bedroom units, 49 one-bedroom units, and 7 studio units), and 79 Class 1 and 8 Class 2 bicycle parking spaces. Approximately 240 square feet of private usable open space is provided via balconies for six dwelling units, and 5,700 square feet of common usable open space is provided via an interior court and roof deck. The two buildings are separated by a public sewer easement that will be developed as a 25-foot-wide courtyard open space as an extension of Verdi Place. The project utilizes Planning Code Section 207(c)(9), commonly known as Cars to Casas, to achieve an exemption to the dwelling unit density limits. ard.

Located on the ground level of an existing two-story building is a vacant commercial/retail space totaling at 2,518 sq. ft. Pursuant to Planning Code Section 249.25(2)(a), the project seeks a Conditional Use Authorization for a change of use from Retail to Office Use at the ground level. This project only seeks to memorialize the change of use and does not propose any alterations, construction, or expansions of any kind.

The project proposes to demolish an existing commercial building to construct a new eight story, approximately 88-foot-tall, 31,912 square foot residential building. The Project includes 20 dwelling units (12 two-bedroom units and eight three-bedroom units), eight Class 1 and two Class 2 bicycle parking spaces, and a below grade garage with 18 off-street parking spaces. 

Pursuant to California Government Code Sections 65915 (State Density Bonus Law), the project requests six waivers for floor area ratio (Sec. 124), rear yard (Sec. 134), residential open space (Sec. 135), bicycle parking (Sec. 155.2), better roofs (Sec. 149) and height (Sec. 260); and one incentive/concession from development standards for permitted obstructions (Sec. 136).

The proposed project at 450 Pacific Avenue consists of improvements to support its continued office use; remove the existing metal fencing and gate along Pacific Avenue, the non-historic storefront and entry, and the metal gratings in front of many windows along the building’s Osgood Place frontage. New storefront systems and an entry would be installed within the same building openings, though at the approximate location of the existing fencing rather than at the setback storefront, and the windows along Osgood would remain unobscured.

The proposed project is limited to the replacement of the three easternmost non-historic storefronts. The proposed storefronts will be built within the existing historic openings. No original fabric will be removed and the historic character of the building will be retained. The proposed storefront design will have full-height glass with vertical steel mullions that are rhythmically spaced. The storefront will also have a horizontal steel mullion at the location of a transom line and another horizontal steel mullion at the lower portion of the storefront. The panels below the lower horizontal mullion are proposed to be steel and will have the appearance of a bulkhead. The storefront will rest on the existing concrete base which is low in height.  The entry door to the restaurant seating area will be located at the second bay from the east end and will be a framed door with a glazed panel. This portion of the storefront (7’-6” in length) will be set back to prevent the door from crossing the property line as it swings out. The third bay from the eastern end of the building will have an entry door to the restaurant’s kitchen. This door will be a solid metal door with a painted metal surround. The storefront glazing in this bay will be back-painted approximately halfway up the storefront to hide back of house storage.

The proposed storefront will be compatible with the District through the use of painted steel, a material found throughout the Jackson Square Historic District. The new storefront design will also be compatible with its reference to both a bulkhead and transom line. The storefront mullions convey verticality, a characteristic that is compatible with typical punched windows in contributing buildings in the District.

The project proposes a change of use pursuant to Planning Code Section 202.11 to allow office use on the first floor and basement of 402 Jackson Street. The completed project will result in a building entirely dedicated to office use. No additions or exterior alterations are proposed.

Certificate of Appropriateness request for work at adjoining properties 809, 831, and 845 Montgomery; 530 Jackson Street; and 100 Columbus Avenue. At 809 Montgomery Street, work includes installation of one new window at the secondary north elevation at the second floor, installation of a new skylight on the roof, and interior alterations related to internally merging this building with 831 Montgomery Street. At 831 Montgomery Street, work includes replacement of the non-historic brick-veneer cladding and storefront enframement at the Montgomery Street façade with new brick veneer cladding, replacement of the non-historic storefront infill and entrance security gate with new multilite steel-and-glass storefront infill, removal of a non-historic rear one-story addition, installation of a one-story rear exterior egress stair at the basement level leading to the ground level, installation of two new skylights, and interior alterations related to internally merging this building with 809 Montgomery Street. At 100 Columbus Avenue/845 Montgomery Street, work includes modification of the proposed previously approved steel-and-wood open rear egress stair, which is physically attached to the rear of 809 Montgomery Street but is located in the rear open areas of 845 Montgomery Street and 100 Columbus Avenue, to have a smaller overall footprint, incorporate an internal ADA chair lift, and add glass railings. At 530 Jackson Street, work includes replacement of seven non-historic aluminum and wood windows with new aluminum windows at the rear north elevation and the secondary west elevation in connection with fire safety requirements for the construction of the open rear egress stair for 809 Montgomery Street.

On Level 5, the existing exterior terrace will be renovated. The work includes replacing the two existing framed glass doors with sliding framed glass panels and adding a new cantilevered trellis, along with new planters and benches. The project also proposes replacing select portions of the existing non-historic stucco cladding at the south elevation of Level 5. The non-historic metal railing at the Level 5 terrace will be replaced and a skylight in the terrace floor will be removed/infilled. Select non-historic skylights at the roof will also be removed/infilled.

The project will adhere to the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards and ensure the historic integrity of the building (Levels 1-4) is maintained. The proposed improvements will not affect or remove any of the building's character-defining features at Levels 1-4. Level 5 was added in 1998 and does not contain any character-defining features.

Certificate of Appropriateness to permit replacing the existing non-historic storefronts at the ground floor with new compatible storefronts. The proposed storefronts will be compatible in materials and proportions. Additionally, the existing non-historic window units on the building's south (street facade) and west elevations (floors 2 - 5) will be replaced.  The existing painted brick surface on the south elevation will be repainted. All historic features of the building will be retained and protected. The project will adhere to the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards and ensure the historic integrity of the building is maintained. The proposed improvements will not affect or remove any of the structure's character-defining features.

The scope includes replacing the existing non-historic security fence with a frameless glass storefront, removing the rectangular windows and frames below the arched windows and refinishing the openings, and reusing the two historic wooden doors at both ends of the vestibule. The ceiling lights will include new LED fixtures and new tile flooring over the existing concrete slab is proposed.

The project site at 1728 Larkin Street, Assessor’s block and lot 0186/049, consists of a 3,491-square-foot rectangular lot currently improved with a one-story garage structure that was constructed in 1905 in the Nob Hill neighborhood. The extant garage is not a historic resource or a contributor to a historic resource district (Preservation Team Review Form, 1720-1724 Larkin Street, 9/28/2018). The project proposes to demolish the existing single-story garage structure and construct a 13,195-gross-square-foot (gsf), six-story, approximately 61-foot-tall (68’-11” tall to top of elevator penthouse) residential building with six dwelling units. The proposed six dwelling units would consist of one 1-bedroom unit, three 2-bedroom units, and two 3-bedroom units. The project would include an approximately 1,417 gsf garage on the basement and ground levels for six off-street parking spaces including one accessible space. The proposed garage would utilize a four-car parking stacker and be accessed from a 9-foot-wide curb cut on Larkin Street. Six class 1 bicycle parking spaces and two new electric vehicle charging stations would also be located on the ground floor. One new street tree would be installed along the frontage on Larkin Street. The project contains approximately 2,030 square feet of open space via private decks and a common roof deck. The project proposes to excavate approximately 865 cubic yards and install a reinforced mat concrete foundation with helical piers. 

Modified Project Description (9/17/2024): The modified project includes an increase in excavation, additional backyard retaining walls, and additional shoring. The proposed basement space has increased from 1,354 gross square feet to approximately 2,457 gross square feet.

rows.description_planning: The 9,453-square-foot project site is located on the block bound by Washington, Jackson, Leavenworth and Jones streets in the Nob Hill neighborhood of San Francisco. A 28-foot-tall, two-story, 18,906-square-foot public parking garage with 48 vehicle parking spaces, built in 1920, currently occupies the site.  The proposed project would demolish the existing building and construct an approximately 65-foot-tall, six-story-over-basement, 47,329-square-foot residential building with 25 dwelling units (12 one-bedroom units, 9 two-bedroom units, and four three-bedroom units). The project would also include 25 unbundled vehicle parking spaces and 25 bicycle parking spaces in a basement garage. A new 10-foot-wide curb cut on Washington Street would provide access to the new garage, replacing the existing 64-foot-wide curb cut. A main entrance along Washington Street would provide pedestrian access to the building lobby. Two bicycle parking spaces and four new street trees would be installed in the public right of way along the Washington Street frontage. The project would include 6,078 square feet of open space for building residents in a combination of private roof terraces and rear yards, and a common roof deck.  The new building would be supported by a mat or spread footing foundation. Construction would last approximately 18 months and include excavation of the entire site to depths of 13.5 to 20.5 feet below ground surface (from front to back of site) resulting in the removal of approximately 5,100 cubic yards of soil.

The project proposes minor exterior facade work and renovation of an existing eight-story, 118,865 square foot office building lobby space. The exterior facade work consists of the following: staining the exterior red brick veneer; repainting painted metal trim; reconfiguring the space to provide for additional commercial retail space facing the interior private open space; installing new planting, paving, seating, trellis, landscape; and installing a new security gate, which will remain open during business hours. The existing office lobby space will be renovated with new materials, furniture, and lighting. A Certificate of Appropriateness is required under Section 1002(a)(2) of the Planning Code.

The Project proposes construction of two new buildings: (1) a new 41-story mixed use building, approximately 544-foot tall (approximately 574-feet including mechanical penthouses and screening) containing approximately 375,000 square feet of Office use, 210,000 square feet of Hotel use, and 7,500 square feet of lower-level Retail Restaurant & Bar use, all located at 530 Sansome St and adjacent parcels; and (2) a new Fire Station 13 located at 447 Battery Street site (corner of Battery and Merchant streets) (the “Project”). The Project would require the demolition of the existing improvements on the project site.

Downtown Large Project Authorization for existing nine-story historic building with 55,759 square feet of office and 3,001 square feet of ground floor retail space. The Project proposes to demolish the adjacent single-story retail building at 501-505 Washington Street and a concrete capped, below-grade story at 517 Washington Street and construct a 49,999 square foot office addition (the “Project”). The new horizontal and penthouse addition would extend to the north and west of the Existing Building and would add 49,999 square feet of office space and 2,419 square feet of new ground floor retail. The principal historic street-facing facades of the Existing Building on Sansome and Mark Twain Place will be retained, and the addition has been carefully designed to respect and compliment the character of the preexisting structure.

In total, the Project would result in a new building with 105,758 square feet of office and 5,420 square feet of ground floor retail. The Project will also provide 7,103 square feet of open space. 6,103 square feet of private open space would be provided for the building’s tenants, via a 1,245 square foot ground floor courtyard and a 4,858 square foot roof deck. In addition, the Project will add 1,000 square feet of POPOS, located at the ground level between the new structure and the adjacent Transamerica Redwood Park to the west. The new POPOS area will be designed as a visual extension of the existing Transamerica Redwood Park, while respecting the original character of the Park and the separation between the new and old.

The exterior gateway will be structurally reinforced and restored. No change of occupancy is proposed.

The project site is a 3,571-square-foot parcel in the Nob Hill neighborhood. The project site is occupied by an existing 30-foot-tall, three-story, single-family residence that is approximately 3,050 square feet in size with two off-street parking spaces. Immediately east of the project site is a lower playground area of the Betty Ann Ong Recreation Center that is approximately 6 to 20 feet lower than the subject property’s rear yard. The change in elevation is supported by a retaining wall ranging between 6 to 20 feet that extends the length of the playground. 

Utilizing the state density bonus program, the project sponsor proposes the demolition of the existing single-family residence and construction of a 40-foot-tall (50-foot-tall with penthouses), four-story over basement residential building containing 10 for-sale townhouses and one off-street van parking space. The proposed building would be approximately 12,312 square feet in size. Each of the 10 residential units would be 4 stories and would include a penthouse and roof deck. The proposed front unit along Washington Street would be approximately 2,070 square feet in size with three bedrooms while the nine rear units would be approximately 940 square feet with two bedrooms. The proposed roof decks would include approximately 7-foot-tall privacy walls and there would be a mini-split heat pump (condenser unit) on the roof of each unit.

Access to the proposed units would be from a 5-foot-wide pathway that would step up along the eastern edge of the property. The proposed pathway would include a bicycle ramp. Each unit would be equipped with an exterior hoist to facilitate the moving of furniture and other bulky items from the outside. The project would include 10 class 1 bicycle parking spaces and there would be 1 class 2 bicycle parking space on the sidewalk in front of project site. The existing 13-foot-wide curb cut would be reduced to a 10-foot-wide curb cut. The 6 existing trees on the subject property would be removed and the project would plant two trees in front of the project site. Trash and recycling for the proposed building would be located in the shared garage space located at the street level basement.

The proposed development would be supported on micropiles. The project would require approximately 130 cubic yards of excavation with a depth of approximately 12.5 feet below ground surface. Construction duration is approximately 15 months.

The approximately 6,085-square-foot project site contains four existing buildings containing a total of five residential units and two commercial units. The height of the existing buildings on the project site ranges from approximately 10 feet to 35 feet. 

The project sponsor proposes to demolish the four existing buildings and construct an 89-foot-tall (101-foot-tall with elevator penthouse), eight-story residential building with 33 dwelling units. The proposed dwelling unit mix would be 4 three-bedroom units, 11 two-bedroom units, 14 one-bedroom units, and 4 studio units. The proposed building would be approximately 40,949 gross square feet in size and would include a 6,000-gross-square-foot subterranean garage. The proposed garage, which would be accessed by a 16-foot, 4-inch curb cut on Joice Street, would include 9 vehicular parking spaces and 34 Class 1 bicycle parking spaces. The project would provide approximately 1,693 square feet of private usable open space via balconies and 1,732 square feet of common usable open space via a common roof deck. Project construction would require approximately 2,800 cubic yards of excavation with a maximum depth of approximately 25 feet below ground surface. Construction duration is estimated for 24 months. The proposed building foundation would be drilled piers.

The approximately 7,521-square-foot project site is located on the north side of Sutter Street on the block bounded by Bush, Stockton, Sutter and Powell streets in the Downtown/Civic Center neighborhood of San Francisco. The site includes 75 feet of frontage along Sutter Street. The proposed project would demolish an existing 22,219-gross-square-foot, 38-foot-tall, 2-story-over-basement, brick retail building and construct an approximately 73,000-gross-square-foot,128-foot-tall (142 feet to elevator override),12-story-over-basement,149-room hotel. A roof terrace would provide approximately 3,340 square feet of privately owned public open space. An existing 42-foot-long commercial loading zone (yellow curb) and approximately 14-foot-long no parking zone (red curb) would be removed and replaced with a 47-foot-long passenger loading zone (white curb) and a new accessible curb ramp. No vehicle parking is proposed. The project would include a 755-brake horsepower diesel-fired emergency generator located on the upper roof. The proposed emergency generator would be EPA Tier 2 certified and be equipped with a California Air Board level 3 Verified Diesel Emissions Control Strategy. Construction of the project is anticipated to start in 2023 and last approximately 19 months. This includes the removal of escalators in the center of the atrium and installation of new vertical circulation elements (elevators and stairs) connecting all levels of the Galleria and the existing roof level POPOS. Work includes installation of base building infrastructure for new commercial cooking facilities, new mechanical and smoke control systems, new finishes and lighting throughout, and an enhanced external connection with the adjacent One Montgomery Tower office building. All levels will remain retail use and the proposed work is shell and core only in anticipation of retail uses. No increase in gross square footage or change of use is proposed.

In addition, the proposed project would provide approximately 4,739 total square feet of common outdoor space at the basement level. Five dwelling units on the sixth story would also include private outdoor patios. Two new street trees would also be provided along the project frontage on Post Street.

The existing 35-foot westerly curb cut would be removed and filled in, and the portion beyond the existing bus zone would be converted to a passenger loading zone. The two existing on-street parking spaces would remain. The eastern curb cut would be repositioned slightly, as needed, to provide access to the proposed basement garage. The basement garage would contain a maximum of nine surface parking spaces (including one car-share space) and 80 total stacked class I bicycle parking spaces. In addition, the project would provide six class II bicycle parking spaces on the Post Street frontage. The basement garage would be accessed via a one-way ramp on Post Street. A traffic control device would be installed at the top and bottom of the ramp to prevent vehicle conflicts. Pedestrian access to the residential lobby would also be provided on Post Street. 

Construction of the project would disturb approximately 13,750 square feet of soil and require excavation to a maximum depth of 20 feet below ground surface for construction of the basement level and elevator pit. The project would excavate approximately 4,056 cubic yards of soil. Project construction is anticipated to last 24 months.

The building height would remain unchanged at approximately 153 feet to the roof level (179 feet in height inclusive of mechanical penthouse).  The project proposes a change in use for the conversion of the existing office and retail department store (former Macys) building into a mixed-use building with approximately 63,240 square feet of retail (floors 1-3 + basement floors), 81,470 square feet of office (floors 4-7 and 11), and 49,700 square feet of residential use with 21 dwelling units (floors 8 – 10). Entry  access to the residential units and office space would be from Stockton Street; retail access would be from Geary Street.

The project site is located on the corner of Stockton and Market streets. The project block is bounded by Stockton Street to the west, Market Street to the south, Ellis Street to the southwest and O’Farrell Street to the north. Buildings adjacent to the project site include a six-story-over-basement commercial building to the north (48 Stockton), and the historic ten-story commercial Phelan Building to the east. 

The existing building at 2 Stockton Street is a four-story-over-basement steel-framed building with retail uses on the first three floors (encompassing a total of approximately 71,700 gross square feet) and storage uses on the fourth floor. Originally constructed in 1907 as the retail store, Roos Bros., the 2 Stockton building was remodeled in 1994 to become the Virgin MegaStore. The existing building has been vacant since early 2020; however, one retailer is slated to occupy a portion of the building beginning in 2022 through September 2023. The project site is zoned as Downtown Retail (C-3-R) and is in a 80-130-F height and bulk district. The building is identified as an Article 11 Preservation Designation “Category V – Unrated Building” within the Kearny Market Mason Sutter Conservation District. 

The proposed project consists of constructing 49,999 square feet of office uses through the demolition and expansion of the existing fourth floor and the addition of a fifth, sixth, and partial seventh floor to the existing four-story-over-basement building. Retail use would be located on the first three floors and basement of the building and the upper four floors would be designated for office uses. The top three floors would be set back from the adjacent Phelan building approximately 19 feet. The building roof would contain mechanical equipment, emergency generator, electrical rooms, an elevator, and 2,488 square feet of solar photovoltaic panels. In addition to retail uses, the basement would contain building services and operations, a bicycle commuter facility with 16 Class I bicycle parking spaces, clothing lockers, and shower facilities serving both retail and office uses. No on site or off site parking would be provided. The proposed project would install 14 Class II bicycle parking spaces along the Stockton and Market Streets sidewalks. The three existing street trees along the project frontage on Market Street would not be removed. No streetscape improvements are anticipated.

rows.description_planning:
The 37,734-square-foot (sf) project site contains an existing K-8 school (St Vincent De Paul School), which is located on a block bounded by Green, Pierce, Steiner and Union streets. The project site is part of the St. Vincent de Paul California Parish Complex, which includes three buildings; the main school building (currently used as the lower school) constructed in 1924; and the Gymnasium and classroom buildings (currently used as the middle school) constructed in 1948. The lower school building is 39’-4” tall and 18,856 sf and the middle school building is 42’-4” tall and 5,972 sf. The corner of the site is now a surface parking lot with 25 off-street spaces. The courtyard is also used for parking, with 7 spaces in a carport at grade under the middle school and approximately 10 additional non-striped spaces in the courtyard. The Parish Complex is considered an individual historic resource.

The proposed project includes infill of the first floor of the middle school, and a new addition, including a new stairway connecting the middle school and the lower school. These additions would expand the existing building footprint. The middle school would increase in size from 5,972 sf to 13,650 sf for an increase of 7,678 sf. The building renovation would involve seismic upgrades to the middle school building, and the new addition to the middle school building to connect to the lower school. With the ground floor infill of the middle school, the parking area at the main courtyard would be reduced from 17 to 7 parking spaces. The project would also rehabilitate the existing lower school building. Demolition would include infill of an existing carport, and demolition of the existing west stair tower at the lower school, which would reduce the size of the lower school building from 18,856 sf to 17,028 sf for a net reduction of 1,828 sf. The gym would be reduced in size from 22,579 sf to 21,910 sf for a net reduction of 669 sf. The total net change for the buildings would be an additional 5,181 sf, and the heights of the buildings would remain unchanged.

 The existing parking lot at the corner of Green and Pierce streets would remain, however, the project also includes the construction of a 7,820 sf elevated play area above the existing surface parking. The elevated play area would range in height from 8’ to 11’-4”. The project would also involve the removal of one curb cut along Green Street in order to provide a new pedestrian ramp to access the proposed new entry. Together, the existing school buildings are currently 47,407 sf and would be expanded by 5,181 sf for a new total area of 52,588 sf. The project involves building demolition of 3,088 sf, and new building infill and an expanded building footprint of 8,269 sf. The basement area is located under the gym and middle school buildings and is currently 15,867 sf and would be expanded by 36 sf to a new area of 15,903 sf. Current enrollment at the school would remain unchanged at 360 students.

The proposed project excavation would require 215 cubic yards (cy) cut, 583 cy fill, for a total import of 368 cy. Approximately 5 feet of fill would be added to the main courtyard bringing the finished grade to approximately 82 feet. Excavation of 5 to 10 feet of soil is anticipated for rehabilitation related to the expansion of the basement area. The new building addition would be supported on a drilled pier foundation. These piers would be cast-in-place straight shaft friction piers, with a minimum diameter of 18 inches and extend a minimum of 30 feet below grade, into dense sand or stiff clay. Construction of the proposed project would last approximately twelve months.

The property at 835 Turk Street is a seven-story-over-basement, residential hotel built in 1928. The building occupies the length of the property with the ground floor accessed from Turk Street and the basement floor accessed from the back of the building at Elm Street. Built per 1928 SF Building Law Class C, the building has an open main stair, an additional staircase at the Elm Street side, and a fire escape at the Turk Street façade. Two elevators service the lobby and the floors above. The building contains parking (not striped for ADA parking and clear height less than required for ADA), storage, and mechanical rooms at the basement floor. The lobby level (ground floor) consists of a property maintenance office, parking (not striped for ADA parking and clear height less than required for ADA), a maintenance office, and a laundry room. The floors above include regular units, a one-bedroom manager's unit, and a kitchen/dining/lounge area at the first upper floor. The regular units contain bathrooms but no kitchens. The manager's unit contains a bathroom and a kitchen. The construction is concrete with supporting steel structure, wood floor construction at the upper floors, and wood roof construction.

The basement floor is not in the project scope except as required for improvements to the building. The parking will remain not striped for ADA parking and clear height to remain less than required for ADA parking. The required scope at the basement includes structural brace frames, improvements to the Elm Street side stairs, and removing or abandoning MEP equipment and piping. The ground floor use as a parking garage will be changed to become support spaces for the residential use of the building. At the first upper floor, the one-bedroom manager’s unit and the kitchen/dining/lounge area will be converted to become ADA-compliant. At all residential floors, two units at each floor will be combined into one mobility unit and the remaining space will be used to add a trash room with a new chute.

The existing R2 SRO building with 114 units, including unit #101 currently used as common space, will be reduced to 108 units to provide required mobility units. Unit #101 will continue to be used as common space. Windows will be replaced as needed.

The Symphony is exploring potential improvements to the existing 210,000 gross sq. ft. Davies Symphony Hall. This preliminary application proposes to renovate the Hall and explore expansion of the street level lobby, a new performance park, a new recital hall, an expanded musician support wing, and interior renovations of the main concert hall with a net addition of approximately 55,000 gross sq. ft. of floor area.  

The existing and proposed uses would remain public uses consistent with the Property’s P (Public) zoning designation. The scenario presented in this application would decrease seating capacity in the main concert hall from 2,700 seats to approximately 2,100 seats while adding 400 seats in a new recital hall at the corner of Van Ness Avenue and Hayes Street. Open space areas would increase from approximately 4,600 sq. ft. to approx. 39,000 sq. ft, with several new outdoor terraces. The existing 60-space surface parking lot at Franklin and Grove Streets would be constructed with an outdoor performance park, including building areas for event activities and two below-grade parking levels with 76 parking spaces accessible from Franklin. Two off-street freight loading spaces would be provided off of Franklin and the existing freight loading space along Hayes would be eliminated.  

No changes are proposed to the existing Zellerbach Hall. As a public structure, the project would also be subject to the Arts Commission’s Civic Design Review per City Charter Sec. 5.103.

The project proposes removal of a UDU using 317(c)(7)(B) Exemption for Unauthorized Dwelling Units at the rear of the bottom level of the front building on the property and proposes to restore the space to its original storage use. After a site visit was conducted on 1/14/25 where floor to ceiling heights were measured throughout the unit, it was determined that the UDU did not meet legal ceiling height of 7'6", so therefore qualifies for the 317 exemption. As detailed in proposed plans, full bathroom may remain, but that the kitchen cooking elements and dishwasher will be removed for the UDU removal.

rows.description_planning:
The Project Sponsor proposes modifications to the 1500-1540 Market Street (aka “One Oak”) residential development project, first approved by the Planning Commission on June 15, 2017. As modified, the proposed project (“Project”) would demolish two existing non-residential buildings and a surface parking lot and construct a new, approximately 508,000-square-foot residential building with a tower over podium design containing 541 dwelling units. The podium portion of the building is 14 stories high, with a roof height of approximately 139 feet, while the tower extends to 41 stories, reaching a roof height of 400 feet (or approximately 416 feet inclusive of mechanical equipment, and 436 feet tall inclusive of elevator overrun and rooftop screening). Three underground floor levels accommodate area for accessory off-street parking spaces, Class 1 bicycle parking, and MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing) equipment. The ground floor will contain a community room and leasing office, residential lobby, building support and tenant service spaces, as well as vehicular access, parking, and loading spaces. The upper building levels will house dwelling units and recreational amenity areas. 

In total, the Project includes 135 off-street accessory parking spaces, three car share spaces, one off-street freight loading space, two off-street service loading vehicle spaces, as well as 210 Class 1 and 27 Class 2 bicycle parking spaces. To further activate the ground floor experience, the Project would construct a public plaza and shared public right-of-way within a portion of the Oak Street (Oak Plaza). In addition, the existing on-site Muni elevator will remain in its current location, and a new weather protective enclosure will be
constructed around it.

The Project would necessitate approval of Planning Code Zoning Map amendment to reclassify the whole of the Project Site to the 140/400//140-450-R-4 Height and Bulk District, thereby increasing the base podium height from 120 feet to 140 feet and defining a base tower height of 400 feet on the western portion of the Project Site (Assessor’s Parcel 0836/005).

The proposed project includes seismic, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing upgrades to the existing building. A new security gate would be installed on the north side of the west façade (Franklin Street). Two intake and exhaust louvers are proposed at the existing transom level to address programmatic needs. The proposed project would also include exterior repairs to address deferred maintenance. Repairs are proposed to the brick, terra cotta, wood window trim, and the pedimented temple fronts at the light wells. The project would require approximately 31 drilled piers and 113 cubic yards of excavation.

rows.description_planning:
The project site is located at 2637 Union Street and is approximately 3,500 square feet in size. The site is bounded by Union Street to the north, and primarily residential development to the east, south, and west. The site is currently occupied by a three-story, single-family, approximately 3,680-square-foot residence with a rear yard. The proposed project consists of the following modifications and additions: lifting the entire building by approximately 12 inches to convert the existing entry-level suite into a second dwelling unit; excavating a portion of the rear yard to construct a sunken light court at the rear of the entry level; replacing the existing
floor-to-ceiling windows at the entry level with a sectional door to construct a single-car garage; and adding a new partial third level above the existing upper floor. Upon completion of the proposed project, the four-story building would contain a 4,280-square-foot main residential area and a 920-square-foot secondary accessory dwelling unit. In total, the project would include an addition of 1,520 square feet to the existing residence. The proposed project would demolish the existing one-story building on the 11,680-square-foot project site (previously a Firestone Tire retail and service center) and would construct a new mixed-use residential and commercial building. 

The proposed building would include a total of 42 dwelling units, consisting of 24 one-bedroom, 13 two-bedroom, and five three-bedroom. The proposed building would be 6 stories tall and 65 feet in height to the roof (79 feet to the top of the elevator penthouse) and would contain approximately 55,360 gross square feet. The building would contain 850 square feet of ground-level commercial space, a community room, patio, rear yard, roof deck, and solar panels. The project would utilize the HOME-SF program to increase the allowable number of units and building height from 40 feet to 65 feet tall. 

The proposed project would remove the existing curb cut on Geary Boulevard and would add a new ten-foot-wide curb cut along Wood Street for entrance to a ramp for a basement parking garage. The garage would contain a total of 23 parking spaces, 20 of which would utilize a car stacker, and 43 Class I bicycle parking spaces. 

The proposed project would excavate over an approximately 8,000 square foot area to an average depth of 11 feet for a total excavation amount of approximately 3,260 cubic yards of soil. The proposed project would add two additional street trees (for a total of four trees) along the Geary Boulevard frontage, and six additional street trees along the Wood Street frontage. The building would be supported by a reinforced concrete mat foundation.

The project is a new athletic and physical education facility for a K-12 school, the Schools of the Sacred Heart, with a natatorium, gymnasium, an athletic and physical education program space, and rooftop field.

The project will demolish an existing, mostly vacant commercial building and replace it with an approximately 63-foot-tall, four-story-with-basement athletic and physical education facility with a full-sized pool and gymnasium that will allow the Schools of the Sacred Heart to host competitive athletics in a building that it owns, as well as physical education. The project will also include a rooftop field that will be wrapped in netting and fencing to prevent balls from leaving the rooftop area. The building will be LEED Gold. In addition to the pool, gymnasium, and rooftop field, additional spaces include workout and training rooms, restrooms, changing rooms, storage, an administrative office, a ground floor lobby and student lounge, multipurpose rooms, team rooms, bike parking, and back of house space.

As part of the project, Assessor’s Lots 1091/001 and 032 will be merged, and the new building will extend into a portion of the existing Lot 001. No physical changes are proposed to the existing structure on Lot 001 at the corner of Geary Boulevard and Wood Street.

The project site is located on the north side of Anza Street between Wood and Collins streets in the Inner Richmond neighborhood. The proposed project would demolish the existing two-story, two-unit residential building and construct a new 85-foot-tall (approximately 95-foot-tall with elevator penthouse), eight-story, residential building approximately 15,563 square feet in size with 8 units. The proposed unit mix would be of 5 three-bedroom units, 2 two-bedroom units, and 1 four-bedroom unit. One of the two-bedroom units would be affordable. The project includes a basement level with 5 vehicle parking spaces and 8 bicycle parking spaces. The project would include a roof deck. The project would require approximately 240 cubic yards of excavation, with a maximum depth of 4 feet below the existing ground surface, and a construction duration of approximately 18 months. The proposed building would be supported by a mat foundation with drilled piers. The project is proposed under the Housing Choice–San Francisco (HC-SF) Program.

Revision to 2018-010465PRJ. Originally built in 1898 and non-historic, the project site at 345-349 3rd Avenue is on a 3,000 sq. ft. lot located in the Richmond neighborhood on a block bounded by 3rd and 4th Avenues, Geary Blvd., and Clement Street. The proposed project would demolish the existing dwelling and construct a 7,722-gross-square-foot, 40-foot-tall, three-unit building over a garage. The ground floor will have three vehicle and three bicycle parking spaces. The original curb cut and driveway would be retained with a new sidewalk and street tree. Each of the second, third, and fourth floors will have three bedrooms and open space is provided at the ground floor and roof deck. Excavation to a maximum depth of approximately 3 ft. below grade is proposed for the foundation.

The proposed project involves the remodel of an existing restaurant and offices to incorporate a mixed-use conversion. The existing Formula Retail restaurant, Burger King, will remain while the existing office space will be converted into nine residential units. In addition, a 1.5-story, vertical addition with a total of four stories will be constructed to accommodate the new residential units. The proposed project employs SB-423 for streamlined approval and the California State Density Bonus law to increase the allowable unit density by 80% of base density (five units), totaling nine units. The project additionally requests waivers and incentives to achieve the additional units.

A remodel is proposed to the existing three-bedroom, two-bath unit at the second floor. At the third floor, a remodel is proposed to the existing three-bedroom, one-bath unit to become a three-bedroom, three-bath unit. At the fourth floor, a three-bedroom, three-bath unit is proposed. Exterior scopes include enlargement of the front window bays, removal of the existing rear stairways, addition of egress and private open space decks and stairs, and the addition of a rear roof deck and roof pergola.

The Project proposes to legalize the conversion of the ground floor from commercial use to two residential units, which require variances from 1) rear yard requirements pursuant to Planning Code Section 134; (2) open space requirements pursuant to Planning Code Section 135; and (3) exposure requirements pursuant to Planning Code Section 140.

rows.description_planning:
The approximately 2,395-square foot project site (Assessor’s block 1463, lot 043), is located on Clement Street, bounded by 32nd Avenue to the west, 31st Avenue to the east, Clement Street to the north, and Geary Boulevard to the south in the Richmond neighborhood. The existing corner lot building at the project site contains an approximate 2,395-square foot, 20-foot tall, one-story commercial building constructed in 1919 with full lot coverage. The existing commercial building was used as a dance studio (dba China Dance School & Theatre) with a 1-car parking garage accessed on the 32nd Avenue frontage. 

The proposal is to demolish the existing building and construct a new, six-story, mixed-use building with one ground-floor commercial unit and 10 residential units utilizing the Planning Department’s HOME-SF program. The project proposes five 1-bedroom units, four 2-bedroom units and one 3-bedroom units. The proposed building will have zero off-street parking and the existing curb cut on 32nd Avenue will be infilled. The project requires approximately 350 cubic yards of excavation at a depth of 3-feet for foundation slab footing and 5-feet for the elevator pit. The building after construction of the proposed project will be approximately 70 feet tall measured from the top of the elevator penthouse (61 feet measured from surface of roof) and will have ten bicycle parking spaces, 11,123-square feet of residential habitable space, and 632 square feet of commercial space.

rows.description_planning:
The development will replace the existing grocery store with a new larger grocery store and mixed-income apartments. The ground floor program includes approximately 63,000 square feet of retail space (grocery) fronting Fulton Street along with residential lobby and support functions. Upper floors will provide 562 dwelling units in a mix of unit types. 

The development will include 20% of the total units (112 units) serving 50-80% AMI levels of population.

The project is located in the Sunset District between La Playa Street and Lower Great Highway with Lincoln and Irving Streets to the north and south of the parcel. There is an existing motel and parking lot at the site which will be demolished to make way for a new residential building for seniors, which will also include an Adult Day Health Care Center (Institutional Community Facility). The primary entrance for the apartment building and the ADHCC will be located on La Playa. The project will provide a total of 199 apartment units, nine parking spaces, outdoor spaces, a community space with a community kitchen, amenity spaces, and a tenant improvement space that will be the ADHCC. The apartment includes a mix of studios, one bedrooms, and two bedrooms.

The project includes the following removals: the 1,159 sq. ft. food mart, the 950 sq. ft. fueling canopy covering two fuel dispensers; the underground storage tanks and associated underground piping; and two driveways on La Playa Street. The northeast driveway on Lincoln Way will be widened. The new project consists of a 2,027 sq. ft. convenience store, a 1,451 sq. ft. fuel canopy covering two fuel dispensers, and a 20,000 gallon underground storage tank with a new fuel system. The site improvements include an accessible path of travel to the right-of-way, masonry trash enclosure, site lighting, and landscaping.

rows.description_planning:
The approximately 11.4-acre Saint Ignatius College Preparatory (“the school”) school campus is bordered by 39th Avenue and the West Sunset Soccer Fields to the west, Sunset Community Garden to the north, Rivera Street to the south, and 37th Avenue to the east in the Outer Sunset neighborhood. The campus predominantly consists of 12 buildings (totaling approximately 308,242 square feet), an athletic stadium with four 90-foot-tall lights poles, and a practice field with four 40-foot-tall light poles. The project site, where construction would occur, consists of an approximately 1.9-acre (84,480 square feet) portion of the northern end of the St. Ignatius school campus. 

Saint Ignatius proposes the demolition of five buildings that are grouped together on the northern portion of the project site and construction of an 182,850-square-foot addition to the existing main academic building. The buildings to be demolished total approximately 58,800 square feet in size (ranging in height from one to three stories) and include a chapel, dining hall with kitchen, administrative offices, a garage, and a 34-room dormitory. The dormitory rooms were historically for Jesuit community members working at the school. The dormitories have never been made available to the public as rental units in any manner, and no school staff or members of the Jesuit community have ever paid St. Ignatius rent for the accommodations. Currently, eight members of the Jesuit community live in the rooms, three of whom currently work at the school. With the project, three members would move to a residence in San Francisco owned by St. Ignatius, and five members would move to other residences associated with the Jesuit community in the San Francisco Bay Area. No increase in enrollment or staffing is proposed. With implementation of the proposed project, the overall square footage of campus buildings would be approximately444,242 

The proposed addition to the existing main academic building would be 40 feet tall (50 feet tall with mechanical screen) with three stories over a basement and approximately 182,850 square feet. The height of the proposed addition would match the height of the existing main academic building. The addition would provide new flexible educational spaces, a chapel, dining area, and kitchen. The addition would be setback approximately 36 feet from the north property line (towards the Sunset Community Garden). The project would also construct a new retaining wall and fence at the north property line.  

The project includes a new main entrance along 37th Avenue at the connection between the existing main academic building and the proposed addition; this two-story space would include tiered seating to support formal and informal school gatherings. The connection would occur at all three levels of the building to facilitate circulation between the new and existing areas. The existing vehicular access and service drive at the northern end of the campus would remain to provide access to the west side of the campus. Loading would remain at the northern end of the campus, and the existing trash and recycling area would be moved inside the building.  

The project would remove 13 exterior, off-street parking spaces used by the school near the north property line and eight garage spaces dedicated for the eight Jesuit residents living in the dorm rooms. The 86 existing parking spaces at the southern end of the campus would remain. The project would provide 150 new bike parking spaces (120 class I and 30 class II spaces). The project would not remove on-street parking spaces. The project would plant 13 new street trees in front of the project site on 37th Avenue; three street trees would be removed.  

Project construction would require approximately 37,000 cubic yards of excavation with a maximum depth of 19 feet below ground surface. Construction duration is estimated for 25 months.

rows.description_planning:
The project site (Block 2123A, Lot 017) is currently developed with a single-family house. The project proposes to subdivide the site into three new parcels: Lot A (435 Ortega Street), Lot B (445 Ortega Street), and Lot C (451 Ortega Street). Lots A and B will be roughly rectangular shaped, will front onto Ortega Street, and will each contain a new single-family dwelling. Lot C will be a “L-shaped” flag lot and will contain the existing single-family residence that will be modified with new vertical and horizontal additions. Furthermore, the existing residence on the proposed Lot C will be moved north and will be rotated slightly to reorient it with the lot shape. Lot A would be 2,604 square feet, Lot B would be 2,532 square feet, and Lot C would be 4,142 square feet. 

The residence on Lot A would have four bedrooms and five bathrooms and would be approximately 3,753 square feet in size. The residence on Lot B would have three bedrooms and three bathrooms and would be 3,529 square feet in size with a two bedroom ADU. The residence on Lot C would have four bedrooms and three bathrooms and would be 3,596 square feet in size. Each single-family residence would be three stories (up to 23 feet above grade) and would have a two-car garage.

In addition, the project would remove two existing significant trees on the project site but would add six new trees.
Construction of the proposed project would excavate approximately 3,000 cubic yards of soil over an approximately 8,300 square-foot area to a depth of up to 25 feet below ground. Project construction would take approximately 16 months.

rows.description_planning: The 250 Laguna Honda Blvd. project seeks to demolish the two existing structures and on-site pavement parking to develop a 172-unit, 100% affordable housing project designed to provide permanent supportive housing and large-family housing. The eight-story building will include 35 one-bedroom, 93 two-bedroom, and 44 three-bedroom units with 25% designated as permanent supportive housing for formerly unhoused households. All units will be adaptable or mobility and the ground floor will include a community room, flex room, office spaces, support services, and bicycle and vehicle parking. The project is publicly funded and is utilizing streamlined approval (AB 2162) and the Housing Crisis Act of 2019 (SB 330). The affordability levels will range from 30% AMI to 50% AMI, ensuring deeply affordable options for low-income families and individuals. Supportive services will be provided on site to help residents maintain housing stability, achieve self-sufficiency, and integrate into the community. The lead service providers are Mission Housing Development Corporation and Lutheran Social Services.

rows.description_planning:
The Department of Elections (Department) is requesting approval to install a ballot drop-off box near MUNI’s Forest Hill Station. The proposed drop box at the Forest Hill Station will be one of 34 boxes installed throughout the City. The purpose of the drop box is to provide a convenient, secure method for voters to deliver their ballots to the Department during each election. 

The Department identified this location based on criteria set by California Elections Code Section 4005, which emphasizes that drop-off boxes be located near public transportation. Election law also requires the Department to also consider local traffic patterns and limits to the types of transportation available to voters that could impede their access to a drop-off box.   

Voters often travel past the Station due to the topography and street infrastructure in the area surrounding this location. This common pathway will allow voters in the area to observe the drop-off box and utilize its availability.  The ease of pedestrian access to the location will also facilitate and encourage voters to return their ballots using the drop-off location.

Since the Forest Hill Station is a San Francisco Designated Landmark, per request from SF Planning, the Department is submitting a separate stand-alone application for the drop box at Forest Hill Station.

rows.description_planning:
The proposed project site is located on the southwest corner of Mission and Harrington streets, on the block bound by Harrington Street to the north, Mission Street to the east, Norton Street to the south, and Alemany Boulevard to the west. The proposed project would demolish the two existing two-story commercial buildings, currently an Everything $1.50 or Less store at 4550 Mission Street and a vacant commercial space at 4570 Mission Street, previously occupied by a Payless Shoe Source, and would construct a new mixed-use residential and commercial building. 

The proposed building would include 69 dwelling units, consisting of 36 one-bedroom units, 23 two-bedroom units, and 10 three-bedroom units. The proposed building would be six stories tall and 64 feet in height to the roof (as measured from Mission Street, and approximately 79 feet in height to the top of the elevator penthouse) and would contain approximately 74,410 gross square feet. The building would contain 3,690 square feet of ground-level commercial space. Open space would be provided in private patios on the ground-level, and a common deck with an adjacent stormwater garden. Common open space decks would also be provided on the 6th floor and roof, along with solar panels. 

The project would utilize the HOME-SF program to increase the building height from 40 feet to 55 feet for the 4570 Mission Street parcel, and from 56 feet to 64 feet for the 4550 Mission Street parcel. The project would also require approval of the Transportation Demand Management Plan by the Zoning Administrator, demolition and building permits from the Department of Building inspection for the demolition of the existing buildings and construction of the proposed project, sidewalk permits from the Department of Public Works for modifications to public sidewalks, and a lot merger approval from the Department of Public Works. The proposed project would add a curb cut along Harrington Street for an entrance to a ramp for a basement parking garage. The garage would contain a total of 31 vehicle parking spaces (including two ADA spaces) and 86 Class I bicycle parking spaces. Two Class II bicycle parking spaces would be provided along the Mission Street frontage. The sidewalk along Harrington Street would be expanded from approximately eight feet to 14 feet. 

The proposed construction would require excavation over an approximately 12,510 square foot area to an average depth of 15 feet for a total excavation of approximately 6,950 cubic yards of soil. A total of 10 new trees would be planted, five along Mission Street, and five along Harrington Street. The existing street tree in front of 4570 Mission Street would remain, as would the existing plaque in the sidewalk commemorating the childhood home of Jerry Garcia at the corner of Mission and Harrington streets. The building would be supported by a mat slab foundation with six inches of underlaying drain rock.

rows.description_planning: The proposed project is being constructed for Artists Hub on Market, a non-profit arts entity, and Mercy Housing California, a nonprofit affordable housing organization. The project will consist of two core programmatic elements: 1) Approximately 101 units of 100% affordable housing for artists and their families whose household income is at or below 80% of San Francisco Area Median Income and 2) three floors devoted to fostering a vibrant artist community through the inclusion of a black box theater, rehearsal and practice rooms, and additional services supporting the arts. The existing site consists of two lots, APN #3504-039 (an existing surface parking lot) and APN #3504-040 (and existing 3-story retail building at 1687 Market St.). The existing retail building will be demolished and the lots merged prior to the start of construction. The project will consist of two basement levels, three floors of arts space, and 13 floors of residential use with approximately 101 units of 100% affordable housing. The project will have a mix of approximately 25% studios, 50% one bedroom, and 25% two bedroom units.There will be one two-bedroom unit reserved for on-site property management staff. The affordable housing units will be 100% affordable rental housing units to be deed restricted by AB2011. At street level, the building will include a small residential lobby, a black box theater with approximately 90 seats, and neighborhood-serving cafe. The arts space (approx 28,890 sq ft) will also include offices for arts non-profit organizations, and arts rehearsal space available to the San Francisco arts community as well as building residents. Residential use will start at level 4, where there will be an approximately 1,200 sq. ft. common area for residents (community room, fitness room, laundry). The project is proposed to include a roof garden for residential exclusive use adjacent to a green roof element for storm water ordinance compliance. No vehicle parking will be provided. 110 Class 1 bicycle parking spaces will be provided for residential and staff use in separate basement bike storage rooms, and 9 Class 2 bicycle parking spaces will be provided for public use on the sidewalk. The project's main residential entry will front on Gough St., while the main arts, theater, and cafe entry will front on Market St. The building's exterior is designed to respond to and highlight the arts uses occurring within the structure. The lower three floors fronting Market St.will have highly transparent glass with views into the dynamic theater, rehearsal spaces, and cafe. The residential floors above will be clad in an energy-efficient curtainwall system. Portions of the facade will be clad in back-painted glass to reflect the changing light of the day and seasons. The project is requesting three (3) waivers and one (1) concession under the Individually Requested State Density Bonus application. The building will consist of 17 levels of Type 1 (concrete) construction over two Type 1 basement levels.

rows.description_planning:
The Village was previously approved by the Planning Commission under Application No. 2021-007313, Motion Nos. 21236 and 21237, including the creation of The Village SUD pursuant to Planning Code Section 249.2 and approval of a Conditional Use Authorization for exceptions related to floor area ratio, rear yard, use size limits, street frontage, setbacks on narrow streets and alleys, and, most relevant to this amendment, dwelling unit exposure for 18 of the 21 group housing units. The overall scale of the project and its general mix of uses remain substantially consistent with the previously approved project. The principal programmatic revision is an increase in the number of group housing units from 21 to 36, at the request of the Mayor’s Office of Housing and Community Development, on Levels 4, 5, and 6. As a result of this revision, 31 units now require exceptions from the dwelling unit
exposure requirements of Planning Code Section 140, representing an increase of 13 units over the prior approval. Planning Code Section 315 authorizes the Planning Director to grant exceptions to the dwelling unit exposure requirements for 100 percent affordable housing projects. Additional revisions have been made to the internal program and layout in order to support the increased residential count and better align the project with its supportive service mission. Level 4, which was previously designated for medical office use, has been converted to group housing to accommodate the additional units. The medical office component has been relocated to Level 3, where it will provide behavioral health services that directly support the residential use above. The ground floor program has been revised to include cultural and recreational facilities together with an approximately 3,000-squarefoot restaurant space. The restaurant is intended to operate in a manner similar to Delancey Street, providing community members with job training and workforce development opportunities. Because of this training-oriented mission, the project team believes the space may continue to qualify as a Community Facility use. Level 2 is now proposed to accommodate a Native American technology consultancy and training program. In addition, the previously proposed two-level basement has been consolidated into a single basement level. Taken together, these revisions reduce the project’s overall gross square footage from approximately 45,000 gross square feet to 41,500 gross square feet. The building design has also been refined in response to these programmatic changes. The overall massing has been revised to introduce a 5-foot-1-inch setback along the south property line from Level 2 through the roof. This setback allows for unprotected openings that assist in achieving required light and ventilation minimums for the dwelling units on Levels 4 through 6, while also increasing access to daylight for the Level 2 and Level 3 program areas.
The exterior design and fenestration have been updated to respond to the introduction of residential use on Level 4, with window placement now aligned with the revised dwelling unit layout. Although the ground floor program has changed to incorporate a commercial restaurant, the project will maintain the previously approved ground-floor transparency, the circular eastern expression of the building massing, and the established floor-to-floor heights. The façade material is currently proposed as a patterned rainscreen system, shown in the current drawings as terra cotta patterned panels, although alternate materials remain under consideration. Notwithstanding any future refinement in material selection, the design will remain consistent with the original architectural intent. As the project advances through addenda and construction, the project team will continue to keep the Planning Department informed of any revisions to the exterior façade materials.

The Project site is a 10,083 sqft rectangular lot located within the block bounded by 15th, Valencia ,16th and Albion Streets in the Valencia NCT. It fronts 15th Street (95.125') and is currently improved with a 10,470 gross sqft, two-story commercial building covering 100% of the lot, which was constructed in 1916. The building is vacant and formerlyhoused an automotive service company. There are no current sidewalk improvements or street trees.The Project proposes to demolish the existing building and replace it with a 50-unit all-residential, all-electric 46,739 gross sqft building. The building would consist of a 6-story, 65' tall portion with 5 stories of Type IIA cold-formed steel framing over one story of Type IA reinforced concrete podium with 46 dwelling units, and two, 2-story, 25' tall, Type IIA portions with 2 dwelling units each. The proposed building would reduce lot coverage to 8,456 sqft or 84%. The foundation is intended to be a reinforced concrete slab at grade over torque down piles. No on-site car parking is proposed.The new building proposes the following supply of new ownership condominiums: 21 two-bedrooms, 21 one-bedrooms and 8 studios. The average unit size is 935 sqft. The proposed primary building portion includes 8 dwelling units per level on levels 2-6 with a common area roof deck of 2,756 sqft. The ground level consists of 10 dwelling units between the front and rear portions, as well as the required accessory spaces inc. lobby, bike parking, mail/package facilities, mechanical/utility rooms and exit corridors. Two stairs and one elevator service the front portion. The rear portion is accessed through a common central courtyard via a door accessible from the building lobby and by exterior stairs for the second-level units.Residential open space is provided as both private and common area. All residents would have access to a landscaped deck at the roof level. Private open space is provided through either private balconies or yards.There is no on-site car parking in order to maximize housing and encourage alternative modes of transit. There are 50 Class I bike parking spaces on-site and accessible from the ground floor lobby, as well as 4 Class II spaces on the sidewalk. The existing 3 curb cuts and street parking along the project frontage are proposed to be re-purposed forpassenger loading and commercial and motorcycle parking. Four street trees and sidewalk improvements are proposed.The Project provides 11 on-site BMR dwelling units (27% of the Base Project of 39) with at least 15% at 80% AMI (low income) and utilizes the California State Density Bonus Law. This entitles the Project to a 27.5% unit bonus or 11 units for a total of 50. The Project plans to utilize the available SDBL incentives/waivers/concessions for an increase in allowable building height and to reduce rear-yard setbacks in order to accommodate density bonus units.The exterior design was informed by bay window and ground floor residential guidelines, while the color palette is informed by the Latinx and LGBTQ history of the neighborhood.

rows.description_planning: The project proposes the adaptive reuse of an existing two-story, 14,320-square-foot commercial building at 3175 17th Street to house arts activities, dance studios, and support spaces for the Oberlin Dance Collective ("ODC"). The project also proposes a 5,684-square-foot addition for a new third level performance space and a 1,508-square-foot rooftop terrace at 3175 17th Street. The project also proposes to create connections between the two ODC-owned buildings (3175 17th Street and 3153 17th Street) including three interior connections between the two buildings at the first and second levels. One of these connections would join the lobbies of 3175 and 3153 17th Street to create a larger lobby space and provide access to updated restroom facilities. The project would result in approximately 250 cubic yards of excavation with a depth of 3 feet below ground surface.

The project site is the existing campus of the La Scuola International School at 3250 18th Street. The site is developed with a two-story over basement building known as the St. Charles building, three temporary portable buildings, and a recreational play yard for students at the school. In 2021, a second building on-site (3270 18th Street) was demolished and replaced with three temporary portable buildings. The portable classroom structures were installed on the site pursuant to the Mayor's Executive Directive on schools (Planning Department case no. 2021-006259PRJ). The La Scuola International School has a second campus building located at 741 South Van Ness Avenue; however, no changes are currently proposed for that campus building and La Scuola International School in this document refers to the campus at 3250 18th Street only. 

The project proposes to remove the three existing portable buildings and to construct a new four-story, 20,370-square-foot building in the southwestern portion of the existing play yard. The new building would be 59 feet tall (approximately 68 feet tall including rooftop appurtenances) and would include nine new classrooms, offices, a dining and kitchen area, an occupied roof, and other support spaces. The proposed project would increase maximum student enrollment for the K-8 school from 191 to 475 students and increase the number of teachers and staff from 54 to 96. Additionally, the existing play yard would be reconfigured and would change from 5,223 square feet to 9,681 square feet. In combination with the proposed 1,895-square-foot rooftop open space area and 652-square-foot outdoor deck on the new building, the proposed project would provide 12,228 total square feet of recreational open space. 

Other project elements include 36 class 1 bicycle parking spaces, 14 class 2 bicycle parking spaces, three new street trees on Shotwell Street, and a new ADA-compliant curb cut on 18th Street to provide pedestrian access to the primary entrance on 18th Street. In addition, sidewalk sections along the project’s frontages on 18th and Shotwell streets would be replaced.  The project frontages on 18th and Shotwell streets are currently designated as passenger loading zones during school drop-off and pick-up hours on weekdays between 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. and between 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.; no changes to the existing curb configuration are currently proposed.

The proposed building would be supported by a mat foundation on improved soil. Approximately 7,600 square feet of soil would be disturbed. The mat-slab foundation would be supported by micro-piles and direct drilled sand-cement piles. No soil would be excavated or filled under the new mat-slab foundation. The ground surfaces immediately surrounding the building to the north and east would be raised by 3 feet. Project construction is anticipated to last 24 months.
