The project proposal (“Project”) is to legalize the unauthorized conversion of 66 tourist Hotel rooms on the eighth and ninth floors of the BEI Hotel to 66 residential Group Housing units. The Project is eligible for administrative review as a 100% Affordable Housing Project under Planning Code Section 315 because all of the proposed Group Housing units would be restricted as affordable to households earning 120% or less of the Area Median Income (“AMI”). However, because the Mayor’s Office of Housing and Community Development (“MOHCD”) has not yet represented to the Planning Department that the Project is exempt from the Inclusionary Affordable Housing Program (Planning Code Section 415), the Project will provide additional on-site Below Market Rate (“BMR”) units at the following rates and levels of affordability: 10% of the 66 Project units at Very Low (50%) AMI; 2.5% at Low (80%) AMI; 2.5% at Middle (110%) AMI; and the remaining 85% at Moderate (120%) AMI. The Project seeks one development concession or incentive from the Planning Code’s requirement for residential usable open space (Section 135) under the State Density Bonus Law (CA Government Code Section 65915 et seq.), for which it is eligible through its provision of Very Low Income (50% of AMI) on-site BMR units; and with which it will comply as a “Shared Housing Building,” as that term is defined in CA Government Code Section 65915(o)(7)(A) and (B), through provision of one shared kitchen and a private microwave and refrigerator for each unit. By virtue of its status as a 100% Affordable Housing Project under Planning Code Section 315, the Project is eligible for administrative review and is exempt from the definitional requirement to provide one-half of one square-foot of interior common space for every square-foot of private residential space for the proposed Group Housing units.

The proposed project (“Project”) is utilizing the Individually Requested State Density Bonus Program to achieve a roughly 8% density bonus and includes four waivers from: Rear Yard (Section 134), Exposure (Section 140), Bulk (Sec. 270) and Wind comfort criteria in exceedance (Sec. 148). The Project includes construction of an nine-story, 85-foot tall, 30,000 square foot, residential building with approximately 408 square foot community space fronting Mission Street and residential uses on floors 2-9 . The Project includes 57 housing units. The Project would provide 57 Class 1 and 4 Class 2 bicycle parking spaces.

To Comply with Planning Code Enforcement Case No. 2023-009082ENF. The proposed project is to legalize the change of use from a credit union to group housing. The project complies with group housing requirements as is, except for the need to add a full stove to comply with the Planning Code. There are 15 bedroom equivalent group housing units and 1 kitchen. Also, the amount of common space exceeds the 0.5 feet of common space for every 1 foot of private space ratio required. At least 15% of that common space is in the communal kitchen area, as required.

Aside from the addition of a stove to the kitchen, we are proposing no changes to the as-built condition. We currently charge $700 per month, inclusive of utilities and internet, which is affordable even for those who qualify as extremely low income.

The Project proposes to redevelop the existing Golden Gate University site at 536 Mission Street, located between 1st and 2nd Streets at the corner of Ecker Place and Jesse Street (the
“Property”). The project will demolish the existing seven-story, 236,680 square foot Golden Gate University building (Institutional Use) and construct a new tower on the lot and proposes 46-stories development with two variants. The first is a 700-foot-tall (752 feet to the top of the parapet), 1,354,395 GSF office building (the “Office Variant”). The second variant is a 650-
foot-tall (698 feet to top of the parapet), 1,171,937 GSF building that would include a mix of office and 385 residential dwelling units (the “Mixed Use Variant”).

The project on floors one (ground floor) and two of an existing 22-story high-rise located at 555 Market Street include improvements to the existing lobby space and construction of tenant amenity spaces, conference rooms, and fitness areas. The scope also includes a change of use on level one for a new public-facing bar and restaurant along Market Street. The new bar space will include an outdoor terrace that wraps around the base of the tower podium, which will require the installation of a glass railing around the perimeter of the podium.

The project sponsor proposes to undertake a mixed-use project that includes six major components:(1) New Tower. The existing, almost 474-foot-tall office building at 77 Beale Street would be demolished and an up to 1,225-foot-tall tower with a 75-foot-tall architectural crown would be constructed. The new tower would include primarily office uses but could include institutional, hotel, and/or residential uses, in addition to retail. In addition, the new tower may include an observation deck at or near the top of the tower; (2) 25 Beale Conversion. The existing, approximately 200-foot-tall office building at 25 Beale Street would be converted to residential use, which would result in a range of between 44 to 120 units; (3) Historic Complex Renovation. The existing historic buildings at 215 and 245 Market Street would be renovated, retaining up to 340,000 gross square feet (gsf) for office and/or institutional uses, along with ground-floor retail. The 45 Beale Street and 215 Market Street Annex buildings and the adjoining interior courtyard would be demolished;(4) Retail. Up to 250,000 gsf of new retail opportunities would be created throughout the site, including 13,500 gsf of existing retail in the 215 and 245 Market Street buildings that would be retained and renovated, and up to 236,500 gsf of retail elsewhere in the site including in the new tower, project variant building, and the new open spaces. Up to 100,000 gsf of the retail could be replaced with general entertainment uses; (5) Open Space. New open space opportunities would be created in a new grade-level courtyard—referred to as the “Urban Village”—by demolishing the 45 Beale Street and 215 Market Street Annex buildings, an adjacent courtyard, and the two-story parking garage at 50 Main Street. Programming for the open space may include up to 7,500 gsf of outdoor entertainment uses; and (6) Project Variants. The EIR will also analyze two variants that would include a second 400-foot-tall stand-alone building along the site’s Main Street façade. The second tower could include up to 317 units (300,000 gsf) of residential use (residential variant) or up to 350 rooms (260,000 gsf) of tourist hotel use (hotel variant). Alternatively, the additional residential or hotel uses could be incorporated into the new, 1,225-foot-tall tower.

rows.description_planning: 100 Mission Owner LLC (the “Owner”) proposes to make minor renovations to the existing building, including (1) establishment of a retail café (1,873 square feet) and associated coworking space (4,333 square feet) on the ground floor; (2) renovating the existing office space on the second floor to create a full floor plate, allowing for the addition of 2,422 square feet of office space; (3) constructing a new floor at the top of the building containing a 7,481 square foot restaurant space (and served by a dedicated entry on the ground floor); and (4) establishing an additional 3,890 square feet of amenity space serving the building’s office tenants in the basement. In total, the Project consists of 17,670 square feet of newly built out space and an increase in gross floor area (as defined by the Planning Code) of 8,242 square feet.

The project site at 1 Market Street (Block/Lot 3713/007; lot 006 is not within the scope of this application) has a 151,250 sf lot area and encompasses the entire block bounded by Market, Steuart, Mission, and Spear Streets in Downtown San Francisco (the "Property").  The Property is in the C-3-O(SD) Zoning District,  150-X and 200-S Height and Bulk Districts, the Transit Center Special Sign District, and the Market Street Special Sign District. The Property is currently improved with an 11-story primarily office tower with 434,396 sf of floor area as well as a 43-story primarily office tower and 38-story primarily office tower (both inclusive of 6-story podium) with combined 1,534,312 sf of floor area, totaling approximately 1,968,708 sf of floor area. 

The project proposes to establish a 5,040 square foot non-retail fitness center at the ground floor in Suite XXPL, which fronts on Spear Street, to serve tenants of the Property (the "Project"). The ground floor of the Property consists of twenty-six tenant spaces, with retail sales commercial uses, including restaurants, cafes, salon, bank, and fitness center, and nine vacant tenant spaces, two of which including the subject space have Spear Street frontage. The subject tenant space has been vacant since September 2021. The subject tenant space was last occupied by a real estate brokerage office for approximately eighteen months. Prior to the real estate leasing office, the subject space sat dark for approximately eighteen months after a long-term dental office (Findlay Dental Arts) ceased operations. The subject tenant space is directly adjacent to an existing retail fitness center and from the pedestrian experience on Spear Street will appear as if an extension of that adjacent retail fitness center. 

To establish the proposed use, the Project requires a change of use from real estate brokerage office (a Retail Sales and Service Use) to Office Use (fitness center serving the upper floor office tenant). The Project seeks Conditional Use authorization pursuant to Planning Code Sections 303 and 210.2 to establish a Non-Retail Sales and Service use at the ground floor. 

* Please note, for clarity, the Project and Land Use Table below only includes information pertaining to the ground floor.

The project is seeking a Conditional Use Authorization pursuant to Planning Code Sections 210.2 and 303 to convert a vacant, ground floor retail space to an office tenant amenity space (Non-Retail Sales & Services Use). The project proposes a change of use to convert approximately 3,615 sq. ft. of vacant ground floor restaurant space to a tenant amenity space. The previous tenant, Tokyo Express, vacated the storefront in 2020. The new office amenity area would include a new conference room, break room, phone room, bike storage space, showers, and a lounge area.

A Conditional Use authorization is sought pursuant to Planning Code Sections 303 and 317 to legalize the combination of penthouses 4 and 5, which were merged by the prior owners in 2008.

The proposed project (“Project”) would demolish an existing surface parking lot located at 524 Howard Street
and a four-story, 29,955 square-foot commercial building located at 530 Howard Street and construct a new 72-
story, approximately 795-foot tall (approximately 844 feet inclusive of permitted rooftop appurtenances)
residential building containing 818,922 gross square feet of residential use. The Project includes 672 dwelling
units, with 68 dwelling units dedicated to households earning 50% AMI. The dwelling unit mix is comprised of
424 one-bedroom units, 180 two-bedroom units, and 68 three-bedroom units. The Project includes three levels
of above-grade, off-street garage parking, including 149 vehicular parking spaces, two freight loading spaces, two
service vehicle spaces, four car-share spaces, and 422 Class 1 bicycle parking spaces. Additionally, 34 Class 2
bicycle parking spaces will be located on the Natoma Street and Howard Street sidewalks. The Project includes a
publicly-accessible fifth-floor deck with a walking path connecting to Salesforce Park accessed via elevators on
the Natoma Street frontage. Other amenities available to residents of the Project include a sixth-floor deck, gym,
and swimming pool, as well as a communal lounge and deck on the 70th floor.

The Project proposes the construction of a 61-story, approximately 800-foot tall mixed-use tower containing  a 189-guest room hotel, approximately 276,000 square feet office space, and 165 dwelling units, in addition to 2 mechanical floors, 7 floors of shared amenity space, and a 4-level subterranean garage accessed from Natoma Street via car elevators. A pedestrian bridge linking the Site to the adjacent City Park atop the Transbay Transit Center is also proposed.

The proposed project involves tenant improvements at the ground floor, which is accessed from Howard Street. Specifically, the project includes a change of use to convert an approximately 1,321 square feet of vacant retail use space (d.b.a. the “Slack”) into a video production lab / office use (the “Project”).  The new tenant area will include Anthropic’s media production area as well as provide the opportunity for public facing demonstrations of its products.  The media studio will be used for recording company podcast interviews and web content. The ground floor location is the best one as it allows Anthropic  to maintain security and privacy for staff on the upper floors, which is a significant concern in the rapidly evolving AI space as well as it provides easier access for visiting press and guest speakers.
 
The former retail space was never activated by its previous tenant, Slack, albeit the space underwent tenant improvements to demise and create a larger 2,727 sqft retail suite by utilizing base building office spaces adjacent.  No other changes are proposed.

The project site at 680 Folsom Street (Block 3735, Lots 013 & 014) has a lot area of 37,195 sq. ft. and is located at the corner of Folsom and Hawthorne Streets in downtown San Francisco (the “Property”). The Property is in the C-3-S and C-3-0(SD) zoning districts, 320-I height and bulk district, and Transit Center Special Sign District. The site is currently developed with a 14-story building that is primarily utilized as office space above the ground floor. The ground floor of the Property is elevated above street level and set back from the frontage along Folsom Street. The uses on the ground floor consist of tenant amenities and commercial space, including a vacant commercial space that was most recently occupied by a restaurant in 2020 (the “Vacant Suite”). 

The project proposes to establish a 2,094 sq. ft., non-retail office amenity space to be used as an employee lounge and shared conference room in the Vacant Suite at the Property (the “Project”). To establish the proposed use, the Project requires a change of use from retail to office use.

The proposed project (“Project”) includes a change of use with both interior and exterior tenant improvements to an existing, 6-story structure containing a non-residential use (office use). The Project would convert the existing, ground-floor freight loading area fronting Clementina Street, a portion of the ground-floor parking area fronting Tehama Street, and an interior ground floor space previously occupied by a retail use fronting 2nd Street into floor area for office use. In total, 9,074 square feet of Gross Floor Area is proposed for conversion from accessory freight loading, accessory parking, and retail floor areas to office use. Two existing garage doors and adjacent curb cuts would be removed, with infill façades to match the building’s existing façades along both street frontages. The Project would modify a third (existing) garage door fronting Tehama Street to accommodate 3 new service vehicle loading spaces, replacing 2 existing freight loading spaces. The Project would reduce the number of existing accessory parking spaces from 50 to 25 spaces and would add 32 Class 1 bicycle parking spaces.

The Project requests Conditional Use authorization pursuant to Planning Code Sections 303 and 210.2 to establish an Office Use (a Non-Retail Sales & Services use) at the Property’s ground floor. The Project will convert an existing 5,017 sq. ft. of Financial Services use along the building's Howard Street frontage on the Property's first floor into tenant amenities, including presentation space and lounge areas.

rows.description_planning:
The project site at 221 Main Street (Block 3740/034) has a lot area of 16,912 square feet and fronts Main Street and Spear Street between Folsom and Howard Streets in downtown San Francisco (the “Property”). The Property is in the C-3-0(SD) zoning district, 200-S height and bulk district, and the Transit Center Special Sign District. The site is currently developed with a 16-story building that is primarily utilized as office space above the ground floor. The ground floor of the Property is elevated significantly above street level. The uses on the ground floor consist of tenant amenities and a vacant commercial space on the Spear Street frontage, most recently occupied by a child care use. The vacant commercial space, Suite 103, is elevated approximately 4'-11" above street level with entry doors set back approximately 45'-4.5" from the edge of the sidewalk.

The project proposes to establish a 4,492 square feet non-retail fitness center at the ground floor in Suite 103 as well as a new building-common lactation room to serve tenants of the Property (the “Project”). To establish the proposed use, the Project requires a change of use from child care facility to office use. The Project seeks Conditional Use authorization pursuant to Planning Code sections 303 and 210.2 to establish a Non-Retail Sales and Service use at the ground floor.

The project scope consists of a change of use within the existing ground-floor commercial spaces, converting retail space into office use with associated tenant improvements. The project would be reviewed per Planning Code Section 803.9(4) for the Article 10 Landmark and will require review by the Historic Preservation Commission to ensure compliance with the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for Rehabilitation.

The project also includes architectural and signage upgrades at eight existing ground-floor entry vestibules within the Hills Plaza complex—identified as the Events,  .Org, Lobby, and Fitness entries. The project encompasses four distinct vestibule types, represented across eight entry locations within the complex. The project will maintain the character-defining features of the building while activating the ground floor with viable, long-term uses. 

There will be no changes to the building’s massing, height, or footprint. No demolition, expansion, or structural modifications to the building envelope are proposed. All proposed work will occur within the existing building envelope and within the existing plaza-level storefront footprint.

The project scope consists of a change of use of 12,172 sqft within the existing ground-floor commercial spaces, converting the existing retail space into office use, with associated tenant improvements. No exterior alterations are proposed, and there will be no changes to the building’s massing, height, or footprint. All proposed work will occur within the existing building envelope. The project will maintain the character-defining features of the building while activating the ground floor with a viable, long-term uses. No expansion of floor area, no new construction, and no exterior façade changes are proposed.
The project proposes to convert 15,812 square feet of existing Internet Service Exchange use to General Office use on the second floor of the existing building. No exterior alterations are proposed.

The proposal consists of the construction of a new 130 foot tall, 14-story building with 297 guest rooms, 166,415 sf
hotel; 2,975 sf of ground floor restaurant/bar and related back of house space; 2,350 sf of ground floor privately
owned public open space; and 9,100 sf of off-street parking for 18 valet spaces. The building will feature a 7-
story, 65 foot tall podium with a 14-story, 130 foot tall tower.

The Site is one parcel (Block 3750 / Lot 009) with a parcel area of 11,090 SF. The Site is zoned MUR – Mixed Use Residential with a 130-G height & bulk designation and is located in the Central SoMa Plan Area and the Central SoMa Special Use District. The Site is currently occupied by a 2-story concrete building. The proposed project requires demolishing the existing structure and replacing it with a new building containing (320) Dwelling Units. The Project Sponsor proposes to redevelop the property per the California State Density Bonus Law (California Government CodeSections 65915-65918), into a rental housing project. The proposed project is the "bonus”project, which includes additional density that the Project Sponsor is entitled per California State Law. The "base” project is a hypothetical code-compliant project that conforms to form-based density controls (height, bulk and setback controls), which serves as the basis for calculating bonus density under California State Law.

On January 5, 2017, the Planning Commission approved an Eastern Neighborhoods Large Project Authorization (Motion No. 19828) for a 130', 13-story residential building above ground floor commercial space at 667 Folsom and 120-126 Hawthorne Streets (3750/078, 081 and 082). The approved Project included 8,873 sq. ft. of commercial space, up to 230 dwelling units, 14,050 sq. ft. of open space, and 133 Class I and 15 Class II bicycle parking spaces. Since the Project was approved on May 14, 2020, the Planning Commission approved an amendment of the conditions of approval of Planning Commission Motion No. 19828 to extend the performance period for the Project for three years (Motion No. 20702). The project sponsor seeks to amend the conditions of approval of Planning Commission Motion Nos. 19828 and 20702 to extend the performance period for three years. No modifications are proposed to the Project as originally approved in January 2017.

rows.description_planning: The proposed project is to add five (5) stories of office as well as a green roof and a commonly-accessible rooftop deck. The first-floor office and basement-level will remain. Currently, the Project site contains 13,505 gross square feet ("gsf") off office use, 9,965 gsf of which will remain. The 3, 540 gsf mezzanine level currently used as office is proposed to be eliminated. The Project will add 49,995 gsf of office at the site, for a total of 63,239 gsf of office. Although the Project will eliminate two off-street parking spaces int he basement, the Property's off-street service vehicle spaces will remain.

The project includes demolition of two vacant Production, Distribution and Repair (PDR) buildings (collectively measuring 22,842 gross square feet), adjusting the existing lot line, to accommodate two separate projects, the Project and a separate project to be located at 77 Stillman Street, on two separate parcels (each parcel will measure 8,622 gross square feet). The Project (consisting of one seven-story, 85-foot tall, mixed use building located at 474 Bryant Street) will consist of up to 49,999 square feet of Office use on the upper six floors over approximately 8,566 square feet of Light Manufacturing use on the ground floor and a basement garage. The garage includes 6 parking and loading spaces for the proposed PDR use. A total of 36 Class 1 and four Class 2 bicycle parking spaces are provided.

The project includes demolition of two vacant Production, Distribution and Repair (PDR) buildings (collectively measuring 22,842 gross square feet), adjusting the existing lot line to accommodate two separate projects, the Project as well as a separate office building located at 474 Bryant Street on two separate parcels (each parcel will measure 8,622 gross square feet).  The Project (consisting of a seven-story, 85-foot tall, mixed-use building located at 77 Stillman Street) will consist of  49,834 square feet of Office use on the upper six floors over approximately 8,566 square feet of Light Manufacturing use on the ground floor and a basement garage. The garage includes 14 parking spaces for office tenants and 6 parking and loading spaces for the proposed PDR use. A total of 36 Class 1 and four Class 2 bicycle parking spaces are provided.

The proposed project includes demolition of two existing commercial structures with a combined area of 35,625 sq. ft., the merger of two parcels and construction of a new  84-ft. tall, nine-story and approximately 140,280 sq. ft. residential building with up to 144 dwelling units (consisting of 60 studio, 25 one-bedroom, and 59 two-bedroom units), a combined 10,800 sq. ft. of private open space throughout the building and common open space at a rooftop deck and solarium, and a 17,720 sq. ft. basement garage for 72 accessory auto parking spaces that are accessed through one driveway on Beale Street, and 111 Class 1 bicycle parking spaces. In connection with the proposed project, approximately 1,939 square feet of existing open space would be converted to an outdoor child play area.

The project proposes converting the existing building from office (94,657 square feet) to self-storage (83,935 square feet). No expansion to the existing building envelope is proposed. The project involves demolition of a 6,048-square-foot (sf) commercial building and a 30,000 sf surface parking lot and construction of a 355,630 sf, 12-story, 185-foot-tall building. The building would contain 269,296 sf of office use, 12,506 sf of art-focused PDR use, 3,272 sf of retail sales and service use, a 5,391 sf childcare facility, 24 vehicle parking spaces, six commercial loading spaces accessed via Freelon Street, 85 bicycle parking spaces, and 9,825 sf of rooftop open space. A 30-foot-wide mid-block alley along the east side of the lot would contain 5,602 sf of public open space (POPOS) and 2,250 sf of childcare outdoor space.
The project proposes change of use from autobody shop to PDR to comply with NOV # 2022-008123ENR under BPA # 2023-01039624. Deferred submittal MEP & Tenant improvement.

The proposed project’s base density could be maximumly developed as a four-story, 48-foot group housing residential building with a residential gross floor area of 67,652 sq. ft. and a total gross floor area of 83,999 sq. ft. The Project would seek a 50% density bonus under the individually requested state density bonus program to construct a 127,467 sq. ft. seven-story-over-basement residential building with ground floor retail. In order to achieve that bonus, 15% of base project units must be subject to 50% AMI, which covers the project’s on-site inclusionary requirement at the very-low-income level.  The project will also provide 4.5% of base project units at low income and 4.5% of base project units at moderate income.

rows.description_planning: The project proposes a vertical extension over the existing two-story, commercial building to add a three-bedroom, residential unit. The scope also includes repairs to the fire-damaged area, new construction for a means of egress (stairs), and a new elevator. The project would result in approximately 12 cubic yards of excavation with a maximum depth of 5 feet. The project also proposes a change of use from Beer Manufacturing and Tasting (Light Manufacturing Use) to Office Use and a change of use from Screenprinting (Light Manufacturing Use) to a Restaurant use on the ground floor.

The proposed project (“Project”) is located on an approximately 2.6-acre development lot, which is identified as a “key development site” in the Central SoMa Plan Area. The Project will subdivide the site into three separate parcels. The western and central parcels will be 43,670 square feet (“sf”) and 47,580 sf respectively, for a combined total area of 91,250 sf. The easternmost parcel, sized 22,690 sf, will be dedicated to the City for future affordable housing development.

The Project proposes new construction of two separate high-rise residential buildings – one on each of the two westernmost parcels – including a total of approximately 1,777,000 sf and 1,500 dwelling units. The western building will be 599’ tall and contain approximately 914,000 sf, including a 2,035 square-foot ground floor commercial space, and 785 dwelling units; the eastern building will be 528’ tall and contain approximately 863,000 sf of residential use and 715 dwelling units. Both buildings will include residential uses at grade with associated building support spaces, and parking and loading access. Each building will incorporate parking on four levels, totaling 465 off-street  parking spaces and 450 Class 1 bicycle parking spaces across both buildings. Residential floors above will consist of dwelling units and residential amenity areas, storage, and mechanical support spaces. The buildings are to be separated by an at-grade, landscaped pathway lined with residential units.

The buildings front onto the planned Bluxome Linear Park, a new public park within the Bluxome Street right-of-way spanning the north side of Bluxome Street from Fourth to Fifth Streets, which will be constructed as part of the Project.

The proposed project is a vertical addition to an office building approved by the Planning Commission on December 11, 2014 (2012.1187BCX) and in construction as of February 2016. The proposed project will consist of up to 165,000 sq. ft. of office space on 11 floors above the 6-story base project. The combined buildings (proposed project over existing base project) will have a height of 240', consistent with the Central SOMA Plan. Since it will be built as a vertical addition, no ground will be disturbed for the construction of the proposed Project. Parking, loading, bicycle facilities, and street trees for the proposed project are included in the base building.

The generally rectangular-shaped project site is located at 620 3rd Street midblock on 3rd Street between Brannan and Townsend streets. The project site consists of block/lot number 3787/005. The site is developed with a two-story, 41,680 square-foot warehouse building, which is a contributory structure to the Clyde and Crooks Warehouses Historic District, that is currently used as a data center. The project proposes a third-story vertical addition consisting of 16,296 square feet of office use and the conversion of the existing data center use to office use. In total, the project would contain 49,990 square feet of office space. The proposed project would also include 2,567 square feet of ground floor retail along the 3rd Street frontage, 10 class I and three class II bicycle spaces, bicycle showers and lockers, 943 square feet of private open space at the third floor, and a solar-ready and living roof area. Proposed improvements in the public right-of-way include six new street trees and two new class II bicycle parking racks on 3rd Street, and seven new street trees and one new class II bicycle parking rack on Ritch Street. A new 10-foot sidewalk would also be constructed along the project’s Ritch Street frontage. No diesel backup generators are proposed on-site.

Construction of the proposed project is anticipated to take 12 months. Project construction would not entail any excavation, grading, or ground disturbance, except for the construction of the proposed sidewalks on 3rd Street and Ritch Street and 30 cubic yards of soil disturbance for an elevator pit. Construction equipment staging would primarily occur in the adjacent parking lot to the northwest of the subject building. Intermittent sidewalk or traffic lane closures may be required to move construction equipment and construct right-of-way improvements.

The Project is a modification of a proposal that was approved by the Planning Commission on June 20, 2019 under Large Project Authorization Motion No. 20470 and Conditional use Authorization Motion No. 20471 to construct a mixed-use development with office, hotel, retail, and residential uses . As modified, the current Project includes the demolition of three existing buildings and associated parking lots on a 71,290 square foot development lot and construction of one new building that appears as two towers measuring approximately 380 feet and 400 feet tall, respectively, to the top of the roof, and 405 feet and 435 feet to the top of the mechanical screens. The Project measures approximately 1,042,451 gross square feet, with 1,032,528 square feet of residential use consisting of 1,105 dwelling units (129 studios, 539 one-bedrooms, 400 two-bedrooms, and 37 three-bedrooms), approximately 9,857 square feet of ground-floor retail, 33,996 square feet of privately accessible open space (including 391 private balconies and three commonly accessible rooftop open spaces), and a 9,153-square foot outdoor Privately Owned Public Open Space (POPOS). The Project also includes an approximately 140,000 square-foot, below-grade, two-level basement containing building amenities, six off-street loading spaces, 271 parking spaces, 13 car-share spaces, 352 Class 1 bicycle parking spaces, retail operations, a refuse handling area, and other back-of-house features such as mechanical equipment required for operation and maintenance of the building.
To erect a 3-story, type 1a, parcel delivery service building w/ accessory office, retail spaces & publicly accessible open space. (the project proposes to merge 7 lots into a single lot)

The project proposes to convert some of the exiting building and exterior surface parking area from existing light manufacturing/ R&D use to Fleet Charging, with installation of up to 15 electric vehicle (EV) chargers. The proposed EV chargers would be installed either within the existing building (without requiring any excavation) or in the parking lot (also without excavation or with minimal amount of removal of the existing asphalt), or both.

The Ordinance proposes a modification to the PDR-1-D zoning table to allow Personal Services and School use at the 99 Rhode Island Street property with no limitation on size (2024-008953PCA).

Hiba Academy Bay Area proposes a change of use from a vacant office building to a private school. The school would accommodate up to approximately 500 students (pre-kindergarten to fifth grade). The project would convert the existing parking lot into a surface play area. An additional outdoor play area would be provided on the roof. Building expansion is not proposed.

The project site consists of 4 buildings on lot 004: A, B, C, and E. The existing 2,650-square-foot Building B is proposed to be demolished and replaced with a 9,012-square-foot building that would be tied into the adjacent Buildings A and C. Approximately 13,448 square feet of existing space on the fourth and fifth floors of Buildings C and E would be converted from Light Manufacturing to General Entertainment use. The proposed project also includes the following: renovation of Buildings A, C, and E, specifically interior alterations throughout; installation of new off-street parking spaces accessed from 15th Street; and new storefront and entrance systems.

The proposed project would renovate, rehabilitate, and seismically retrofit the existing 29,500-square-foot historic building at 1200 15th Street to provide office and operational space for use by the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) Parking and Traffic Enforcement Division. The project would also install one temporary trailer (size to be determined) to house the division’s emergency-related operations. Six electric vehicle (EV) parking spaces with EV charging stations would be installed on the ground floor of the existing building and 34 electric bike parking spaces with charging stations would be installed in the yard to accommodate SFMTA fleet vehicles. The project would add 425 public employees to the site. The project would include streetscape improvements around the site. See plans dated April 29, 2022 (site plan revision 01). Project construction would be managed by San Francisco Public Works (PW) and would incorporate the PW standard construction measures as indicated.

See attached project description memo for full project description.

The existing building is a concrete and steel, two-level, mixed-use structure with commercial and childcare uses. Per 2021-005803PRJ and 202105240917,  the Planning Department previously approved a project that proposed the alteration of the existing building, resulting in a structure that maximizes the height and bulk limits on the site (58-X and 68-X). The building was tiered with four levels on the north side of the property and five levels on the south. The approved use of the new building is laboratory use. The proposed structure of the additional levels would be steel and concrete and generally maintain the footprint of the existing building, although the north wall of the existing building was to remain (avoiding a "demolition" per the Planning Code). 

The new project proposes to modify the existing approved project by conducting a full demolition of the entire existing building. There are no existing industrial uses in the building and, therefore, no industrial use placement is triggered.

The Property contains a five-story 1912 building with a three-story and a two-story addition. The Project Sponsor is currently seeking Article 10 Landmark designation for the Property. Once designated, the Property becomes eligible for the Vertical Controls for Office Uses pursuant to Planning Code Sections 210.3B and 803.9(f). The proposed project entails a change in use from PDR (Production, Distribution and Repair) to office use on the third and fourth floors (totaling approximately 22,580 square feet), The Zoning Administrator has determined that there is 12,333 sf of existing, legal non-conforming office space at the building of which 9,655 square feet will be shifted to the fifth floor and 2,007 sf will be shifted to the third floor.

The project proposes to expand 12,333 sq. ft. of legal non-conforming office space at the ground floor to include a 1,059 sq. ft. area that is currently used as a vestibule and bathroom. The project would expand the legal non-conforming office use to 13,392 sq. ft. at the ground floor of the property, an increase of approximately 8.6% in area. No request for expansion of non-residential, non-conforming use has been previously requested for the property. A Conditional Use Authorization pursuant to Planning Code section 181(i) is required for the project.

This proposal is a modification of the project that was approved by the Planning Commission on September 22, 2016 under Case No. 2013.0517ENX. The new project will utilize the State Density Bonus Program to construct a six-story, 70-foot-tall, 73,830-gross-square-foot residential building with 64 dwelling units.

Modification to a previously approved project.

The project was approved under SB 330 and SB 35 and State Density Bonus law for 450 group housing units with 185 units of affordable housing with 41 units earning up to 55% AMI, 129 units earning up to 80% AMI and 15 units earning up to 110% AMI. The project now seeks to modify the existing approval to reduce the total unit count to 425 units with 100% of the units restricted as affordable as follows:  45 units at 30% AMI, 45 units at 50% AMI, 252 units at 60% AMI, 45 units at 70% AMI and 63 units at 80% AMI or less.   This modification results in a 5.6% decrease in unit count 

The project also seeks to modify the total square footage by reducing the development from 12 story building to an 11 story building, resulting in a reduction in GFA of 8.3%

MOHCD AMI levels as of 4 Feb 2026: 58 @ 40%; 150 @ 80%; 217 @ 100%

The site is steeply sloped at approximately 10% along Pennsylvania Avenue. The main residential entry is at the first story near the street intersection. Residential services and amenities, including community room, property, manager and social services offices, bike parking, building utilities and storage are located on the first story. The second story includes residential units as well as the laundry room, ancillary community room, and an exit from the stories above. The third story includes residential units, a family day care unit, and the electrical room. The fourth through ninth story are similar and primarily contain residential units. The roof contains building utilities within an enclosed mechanical penthouse or visual / acoustical enclosure, a vegetated roof to mitigate stormwater, and photovoltaic panels. Additional open space for stormwater treatment and for the family day care is located at level 3 at the south end of the site.

The site is currently vacant with no existing uses or structures. The site is partially excavated and retained and contains existing retaining walls, shoring, slabs on grade, and perimeter fencing.

The proposed project would involve development of a 28-acre site into a mixed-use development, including parks, roads, and infrastructure. Below is a breakdown of the use types of the pier 70-waterfront site development. 

Residential – Development of a range of 2,000 to 1,000 new dwelling units consisting of approximately 1,712,000 - 903,000. As part of this residential program, Building 2 would be rehabilitated into approximately 120 dwelling units (consisting of approximately 110,000 gsf).

Commercial Office – Construction of a range of 1,810,00 million gsf to 900,000  gsf of Class A Office and Research/Development space. As part of the commercial development, a portion of Building 12 would be rehabilitated into commercial office space (consisting of approximately 60,000 gsf).

Retail and Arts – Construction of up to 400,000 gsf of new ground floor commercial retail and arts activity space, including small scale local production and small business incubator uses. Approximately 120,000 gsf of the retail and arts space would result from the construction of Buildings E-1A and E-1B, and approximately 115,000 gsf would result from the rehabilitation of
Buildings 12 and 21.

Parking – The proposal would provide parking within up to three newly-constructed district parking facilities and/or dispersed within buildings housing other uses, based upon the following
maximum rates:
o Residential Condominium Units: 1.0 space per dwelling unit;
o Residential Rental Unit: 0.5 space per dwelling unit;
o Commercial (includes office, restaurant, retail and arts, and all other uses): .9 spaces per
1,000 gsf of floor area

Open Space and Recreation – The project includes construction of approximately seven acres of new public open space and recreational areas consisting of: approximately 3.9 acres for the Slipway Commons Waterfront Park; 0.6 acres for Market Square, located between Building 2 and 12; and, approximately 1.7 acres of useable rooftop open space on the district parking facilities.
¿
Infrastructure Development – The infrastructure development would include a) site preparation, including remediation of contaminated soils, grading, soil compaction and stabilization,

construction and installation of water, sanitary sewer, storm drainage, and utility infrastructure,
and subsurface improvements to improve seismic conditions; and b) construction of streets and
walkways, shoreline improvements, public access, and parks.

The building would include warehouse space, work room, and restrooms. There are a total of 7 existing parking spaces and 1 existing accessible/van parking space. The project would add an additional 17 parking spaces (13 off of 23rd Street adjacent to the existing office building and 4 adjacent to the proposed building), for a total of 24 parking spaces. There is one existing electric vehicle charger, and the project would add 2 additional EV chargers, for a total of 3 EV chargers.

The proposed project would involve construction of up to approximately 5.3 million gross square feet (gsf), and would provide 2,622 parking spaces at a ration of 0.6 space per residential unit (approx. 1,609 spaces in total) and one space per 1,500 sf of commercial office, laboratory, or PDR use (approx. 859 spaces in total) The hotel use would include one parking space for each 16 guest rooms (approx. 14 off-street parking spaces in total) and any grocery store on the Project Site would provide parking at a ratio of 3 spaces per 1,000 sq. ft. of use, approx. 140 spaces in total). Most new buildings would range in height of 65 to 180 ft, with one building at 300 ft. rows.description_planning: Pursuant to Planning Code Section 317(c)(7)(A), the project proposes the removal of a vacant, unauthorized dwelling unit created within an existing non-residential building. The unauthorized unit does not comply with open space or dwelling unit exposure requirements and is ineligible to be legalized pursuant to Section 307, Section 207(c)(4), Section 207(c)(6), or Section 207.3 and is, therefore, exempt from the Conditional Use Authorization requirement. The unauthorized unit was installed within the existing commercial space without a permit and used only by family members of the owner; it was never rented or otherwise occupied by a tenant. As depicted in the plans and diagrams, the unauthorized unit does not comply with applicable open space or dwelling unit exposure requirements of the MUR Zoning District (Showplace Square / Potrero Hill Plan Area). Specifically, the unauthorized unit opens onto a non-residential surface parking lot and approximately 5-foot-wide shared alleyways used for access and egress by neighboring commercial tenants located in other spaces within the property. The project proposes limited interior building demolition; no exterior modifications to the existing commercial building are proposed.

rows.description_planning: Martin Marietta seeks to modernize and reconstruct its existing sand processing facility at Pier 92 by installing new equipment, constructing a new warehouse, paving and reconfiguring the site, and installing a new modern stormwater management system. No changes are proposed to Pier 92 infrastructure or facilities located outside of the project site’s boundaries. The essential nature of the existing operations at the facility would not change. Rather, the proposed project would allow for the existing operation to continue on a redesigned site with modern equipment and improved environmental controls. To accommodate these changes, the project proposes to increase the site footprint from 190,229 square feet to 224,600 square feet under a new lease with the Port of San Francisco. The project has also applied for a permit to construct/permit to operate from the Air District, which would allow the facility to process up to 800,000 US tons of sand per year. Construction of the project would take up to 7 months. Facility operations would continue during construction.

rows.description_planning:
The project site has frontages along Hudson Avenue, a dead-end and currently undeveloped street in the Bayview neighborhood near India Basin Shoreline Park. The project proposes a 3-lot subdivision and the construction of three residential buildings with a total of 9 dwelling units and three off-street parking spaces. Each building would be 38 feet tall, three stories with basement, and would contain one regular unit, one accessory dwelling unit and one junior accessory dwelling unit. In total, the project would include approximately 12,641 square feet of residential use and 2,748 square feet of common open space. 

To access the proposed buildings, a new shared public street would be developed as Hudson Avenue where the existing paper street lies. The southern side of the street would be developed with a 9-foot-wide pedestrian throughway with a 6-foot-wide sidewalk and a 3-foot-wide landscaping area (for street trees). The new street would be limited to local traffic and emergency vehicles only with a 22-foot-wide travel lane; street parking would not be permitted. The new street would include street lighting and an emergency vehicle turn-around. A new, raised crosswalk with stripping and sidewalk bulbout is proposed at the bottom of Hudson Avenue where it intersects with Hawes Street. The project would plant three new street trees in front of the project site. Project construction would be approximately 18 months and would require approximately 810 cubic yards of excavation. The proposed development would be supported on a mat foundation bearing in weathered bedrock.

rows.description_planning:
The project consists of the merger of Assessor's Parcel Numbers (APNs) 4827-003 and 4827-001, located at 1225 and 1205 Van Dyke Avenue, respectively, to allow continued operation and consolidation of an existing construction and demolition debris (CDI) transfer/processing facility and junk yard operation. Both parcels are developed industrial properties located within an established industrial area. Prior to vacating the site, the former tenant at 1205 Van Dyke Avenue operated a permitted junk yard and conducted material handling activities similar in nature to those currently conducted at 1225 Van Dyke Avenue.
 
The project would continue the existing receipt, sorting, processing, storage, and transfer of construction and demolition debris (CDI), including concrete, dirt, wood, metals, cardboard, copper wire, aluminum, and limited quantities of plastic. Materials would continue to be stored outdoors within designated stockpile areas.
 
The project does not involve the development of previously undeveloped land or the introduction of a new land use. Rather, the project would consolidate operations across two existing industrial parcels that have historically supported similar material recovery, storage, processing, and salvage activities.
 
Vehicles delivering CDI would continue to enter the facility from Van Dyke Avenue, proceed to a scale for weighing and load inspection, unload materials in designated areas, and be weighed upon departure to obtain tare weight before exiting the site. Operations would continue to utilize existing material handling and processing equipment, including 226B and 246C skid steers, a Hitachi EX120-5 excavator, and 924G and 938M wheel loaders.
 
The existing facility at 1225 Van Dyke Avenue currently processes less than 87.2 tons of material per day. Following consolidation of the two industrial parcels, the facility would operate as a medium-volume CDI transfer/processing facility with a permitted throughput of up to 166.38 tons per day. To support operational efficiency, the project includes installation of a second truck scale and operation of a shredder to process material suitable for Alternative Daily Cover (ADC), a material used at permitted municipal solid waste landfills in lieu of earthen cover.
 
The project represents the continued operation and consolidation of existing industrial and material recovery activities on developed parcels that have historically supported similar uses. No substantial alteration of the existing site configuration is proposed, and no new buildings or expansion into undeveloped areas would occur.

The project scope consists of tenant improvements to an existing office/warehouse including a buildout of the 2nd level for an open warehouse area and a new stair to the new 2nd floor office and storage area. No exterior, foundation, or structural work is proposed.

rows.description_planning:
The 4,700 square foot project site is located on a down-sloping lot on the east side of Jamestown Avenue east of Griffith Street, with frontage on Jamestown Avenue and on the pedestrian trail portion of Gilroy Street. The proposed project would subdivide the existing vacant lot into three substandard-sized lots, each fronting on Jamestown Avenue. The northernmost Lot A at 778 Jamestown Avenue would be approximately 1,502 square feet, Lot B at 768 Jamestown Avenue would be approximately 1,585 square feet, and Lot C at 758 Jamestown Avenue would be approximately 1,596 square feet.  The project would construct a four-story, 34-foot tall, three-bedroom, single family dwelling on each lot.  Each dwelling unit would have two vehicle parking spaces in an individual, street-level garage accessed by a 10-foot-wide curb cut on Jamestown Avenue and a rear yard. The proposed buildings on Lots B and C would have second-floor rear decks. The project is seeking variances from the Planning Code for three substandard-sized lots and to address front setbacks. Details regarding the lot dimensions and front setbacks are shown on project plans dated December 13, 2018. 
During the approximately 18-month construction period, excavation of approximately 600 cubic yards of material would occur to a maximum depth of approximately 12 feet. 

Foundation Recommendations
Pursuant to the geotechnical investigation prepared for the project (Frank Lee & Associates. February 6, 2018. Soil and Foundation Investigation Proposed Three Four-Story Residential Building 758, 768, 778 Jamestown Avenue, San Francisco, California 94124), the proposed buildings should be supported by drilled piers with grade beams constructed between the piers. The piers should extend 10 – 15 feet into competent soils or bedrock which was encountered at approximately 13.5 feet.
An alternate foundation system that could be used would be a concrete mat slab with a perimeter continuous footing to control moisture migration as described in the geotechnical report.

rows.description_planning:
The Project consists of the redevelopment of the SF Market campus' southeast quadrant lot in the Bayview neighborhood of San Francisco. The general scope of the Project is the demolition of the existing warehouse, dock, and site components and construction of a new core and shell warehouse which will be a produce and food-handling facility. The project will include PDR for use by future tenants, a small operations area, and a food recovery center. The Project also includes on-site horizontal improvements and off-site improvements.

The project site is located on a lot (final Parcel Map is submitted) by Kirkwood Avenue to the south and Rankin Street to the east. The site is bound on the north and west by the Marshalling Yard. The former Jerrold Avenue (to the north) and Selby Street (to the west) right-of-ways are vacated and will be a part of the SF Market marshaling yard via the Parcel Map referenced above. The project site is currently occupied by a two-level warehouse with loading dock.

The horizontal improvements include both onsite and offsite construction. Onsite improvements include utilities, paving and grading, parking and accessible ramps, and storm water provisions. Offsite improvements include the construction of new sidewalks, curbs, gutter, street lighting, planting of street trees, and replacement of street paving where required for utility connections.

The vertical improvements include the construction of one building. The building is a one-story, type V-B, fully sprinklered building with approximately 67,222 sq. ft. of gross building area. The building is approximately 40'-0" to the highest point of the roof.

The proposal is for a Conditional Use Authorization of a Planned Unit Development (PUD) on a site that is over ½ acre and to establish a large-scale retail use over 120,000 square feet, pursuant to Planning Code Sections 121.6, 210.3, 249.22, 303, and 304, for a project that includes the demolition of an existing private parking lot and the construction of a five-story mixed-use building with approximately 150,940 square feet of Self-Storage use,23,460 square feet of Production, Distribution, And Repair (PDR) use, 4 onsite loading spaces, 6 vehicle parking spaces, and 6 Class 1 and 2 Class 2 bicycle parking spaces within the PDR-2  Zoning District,  Industrial Protection Zone Special Use District, and 65-J Height and Bulk District.

The Project requests a modification of the Conditional Use Authorization approved under Case No. 2018-013692CUA (Motion No.20883) pursuant to Planning Code Sections 303 and 210.3 to establish an Internet Service Exchange. There are no proposed
modifications to the PUD that were a part of the original approval but are included as a part of this modification review.

Four buildings are proposed on the two lots with a truck court between the four structures.  Buildings A & B are 4-story structures providing 28' clear dock high industrial space. this industrial space contains a partial level of office located above the loading door. Above the 36' level is general parking for employees and visitors. The level above this contains upper level (UL) industrial. This UL industrial has a 14' high clear space and is served via a common loading dock on the ground level and service elevators.  Buildings C & D are two story structures providing 28' clear dock high industrial space. Each building has a partial level of office located above the loading doors.

The project proposes to construct a new six story, 69-foot tall mixed-use residential and commercial building on a vacant lot. The proposed 25,430 square-foot building would contain 616 square feet of commercial space on the ground floor and 21,780 square feet of residential uses on floors 1 through 6 consisting of 29 dwelling units comprised of eight studios, eight one-bedroom units, 10 two-bedroom units, and three three-bedroom units. The proposed project is a Home-SF project and nine of the dwelling units would be on-site affordable units. The project would include 2,525 total square feet of common outdoor space comprised of a 735 square-foot patio on the ground floor and a 1,790 square-foot rooftop open space. 

In addition, the proposed project includes 32 class-I secure bicycle parking spaces and four class-II bicycle parking spaces on the 3rd Street project frontage, consistent with the city’s bicycle parking requirements. No on-site vehicular parking is proposed. The existing street trees and vehicle parking spaces on the street frontage would remain unchanged. No back-up diesel generator is proposed. 

Construction of the project would occur over the course of approximately 18 months. The project would be supported by a mat slab foundation and would excavate approximately 315 cubic yards of soil to a depth of 2 feet below grade for foundation construction. No pile driving or nighttime construction is proposed.

The project proposes converting the existing ground-floor and rear porch into a new Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit (JADU) and extending toward the rear of the property. The project also includes converting the existing upper-floor rear balcony into conditioned interior space and extending it toward the rear to become part of the single-family main dwelling

The project site consists of six lots (Assessor’s Parcel Number 5411-010, -009, -008, -007, -006, and -005), and is generally sloped, except for the northeastern portion of the property which is flat. The 18,740 square-foot site is vacant except for a double-sided billboard that would be removed as part of the proposed project. 

The proposed project would merge the six lots into one and construct a 65-foot tall, 69,460-square-foot building with 66,130 square feet of residential space and 5,805 square feet of common usable open space, consisting of a 2,090-square-foot rear yard and a 3,715-square-foot roof deck. Additionally, 88 of the proposed dwelling units would have private balconies that would provide usable open space. The project would include 100 dwelling units comprised of 17 studios, 37 one-bedroom, 21 two-bedroom, and 25 three-bedroom units. Of these units, 30 units would be offered at below market rates under the HOME-SF program. The proposed project would not include a backup diesel generator and would not include off-street vehicular parking. Two new street trees and landscaping would be planted along 3rd Street. 

Primary pedestrian access to the residential lobby would be provided on 3rd Street. Consistent with city bicycle parking requirements, the proposed project would provide 100 class I bicycle parking spaces within the building and six class II bicycle parking spaces along the project frontage on 3rd Street. One existing curb cut immediately adjacent to the northernmost crosswalk would be removed and filled in as part of the project. The sidewalk along 3rd Street would also be expanded to 10 feet along the project frontage. 

Construction of the project would disturb approximately 18,700 square feet of soil and require excavation to a maximum depth of 31 feet below ground surface for construction of the building’s mat slab foundation. The project would excavate approximately 12,000 cubic yards of soil. Project construction is anticipated to last 22 months. No pile driving is proposed.

rows.description_planning:
The proposed project site is located east of San Bruno Avenue, west of the Bayshore Freeway, north of the intersection of Ordway Street and San Bruno Avenue, and south of the intersection of Mansell Street and San Bruno Avenue, and is composed of six parcels (block 5478, lots 003, 004, 005, 006, 007, 008). The project site is approximately 25,180 square feet (approximately 0.58 acres) in area. The site contains a billboard and is adjacent to a bus stop, but is otherwise vacant. 

The proposed project would merge the six lots into one and construct three new residential buildings with a total of 45 dwelling units, consisting of a 10-unit, three-story, approximately 10,090 gross square feet (gsf), approximately 29-foot-tall building at 3255 San Bruno Avenue; a 17-unit, three-story, approximately 14,890 gsf, approximately 33-foot-tall building at 3303 San Bruno Avenue; and an 18 unit, three-story, approximately 17,370 gsf, approximately 34-foot-tall building at 3333 San Bruno Avenue. Two of the buildings would include garage-level car parking spaces as follows: three spaces in 3255 San Bruno Avenue and 11 spaces in 3333 San Bruno.

South of 3255 San Bruno, and the existing billboard, the project would include the construction of a proposed open space totaling approximately 8,950 square feet in area zoned as P(Public), which consists of easements for PG&E and SF Water. The existing billboard is located adjacent to the proposed 3255 San Bruno Avenue building and easements are located on portions of all six project site parcels. The easements take up approximately 8,220 square feet, or about 33 percent of the project area. A second open space totaling approximately 1,700 square feet in area would be added south of 3303 San Bruno Avenue and north of 3333 San Bruno Avenue, over the existing PG&E easement. 

The project would be supported by spread footing foundations and require 400 cubic yards of excavation for 3255 San Bruno Avenue, 380 cubic yards of excavation for 3303 San Bruno Avenue, and 420 cubic yards of excavation for 3333 San Bruno Avenue, for a total of 1,200 cubic yards of excavation. Construction is anticipated to take approximately 62 months.

The project would need to relocate the existing bus stop approximately 5 feet south to accommodate the proposed curb cut for 3255 San Bruno. The project would be required to obtain a Street Improvement Permit from Public Works, and would need to coordinate with the bus stop advertiser for removal and installation of the existing bus shelter. The proposed project is seeking a density bonus, as well as waivers from planning code requirements related to rear yard, usable open space, large site citywide design standards, and ground floor residential; and concessions related to curb cuts, affordable housing tiers, and citywide design standards related to residential lobby entries.

The proposal is for the conversion of an existing two-story mixed-used building into ta Religious Institution Use (DBA Or Shalom Jewish Community). The Project seeks to Conditional Use Authorization for the use of 331-333 Cortland Ave for Institutional - Religious Use.  The ground floor commercial unit is currently used as a chiropractor's office. An existing second floor dwelling unit will also be converted into a non-residential use and is subject to Section 317. No physical or structural changes are proposed, with the exception of minor alterations to ensure the building complies with current code requirements for the new use. 331A Cortland Avenue, detached building located at the rear of the property, is currently a dwelling unit (R-3 occupancy) and no changes are proposed.

The project site at 237 Cortland Avenue is an approximately 1,980 square-foot (sq. ft.), lot in the Bernal Heights neighborhood. The project site is located on a block bounded by two sides of Cortland Avenue, Bocana Street, Eugenia Avenue, & Bonview Street. The original cottage was built circa 1885, and has been repeatedly modified into a commercial space with a garage.

The proposed project would demolish the existing commercial space, and construct an approximately 5,617-gross-square-foot (gsf), 40-foot-tall three dwelling over ADU building. The ground floor will have an active street front patio. The original curb cut and driveway would be replaced with a new sidewalk and street tree. Each of the units will have 2 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms. There is a private deck at the rear of each floor, and an unoccupied roof with a solar zone. Excavation to a maximum depth of approximately 3 feet below grade is proposed for the foundation.

rows.description_planning:
The Project (“Project”) includes demolition of the existing abandoned greenhouse structures and new construction of 31 three-story residential duplex buildings with a height of approximately 35 feet and a total Gross Floor Area of approximately 118,600 square feet with ground floor garage and storage spaces. The Project would construct a total of 62 dwelling units. The Project includes 62 off-street vehicle parking spaces, 93 Class 1 and 12 Class 2 bicycle parking spaces. The Project will also provide approximately 43,300 square feet of open space. Of that total amount, approximately 14,900 square feet will be private rear yards, approximately 11,200 square feet will be common shared spaces for the residential units, and approximately 17,200 square feet will be provided as a publicly accessible open space at the corner of Woolsey and Hamilton Streets. As part of demolition, the Project Sponsor would salvage materials from the original boiler house and greenhouses as feasible.

The Project would also add a new 11-foot wide sidewalk along Wayland Street and fill an existing trench to create a new 10-foot wide sidewalk along Bowdoin Street. The existing sidewalks on Hamilton and Woolsey streets would be replaced with 10-foot wide sidewalks and would add four new sidewalk bulbouts (one at each corner of the site). The Project would include 31 new curb cuts and provide approximately 28 on-street parking spaces surrounding the Project site. Two on-street car share spaces will be located on Hamilton Street near the proposed publicly accessible open space. A total of approximately 33 street trees would be provided along the perimeter of the block. (11-8-21 kjd)

rows.description_planning:
The proposed project would demolish the existing commercial structure at 5425 Mission St (lot 19A) and surface parking lot (lot 19) on-site and merge the two lots to construct a five-story over basement, 45-foot mixed-use structure with 29 units, 388 sf of commercial space on the ground floor, and a basement parking garage with 12 off-street parking spaces. The proposed dwelling unit mix consists of, 17 one-bedroom units, 11 two-bedroom units, and one three-bedroom unit. Of these 29 units, six of the units would be inclusionary affordable units. The project would apply the provisions of HOME-SF Guidelines. No backup diesel generator would be located on-site.

With regards to common open space, the project would provide 1,489 square feet of common open space on the third floor and 2,644 square feet of common open space on the rooftop deck; in total, the project includes 4,133 square feet of common open space. In addition, seven new street trees would be planted on the project’s frontage along Mission Street and Florentine Avenue. Primary pedestrian access to the residential lobby would be provided on Florentine Avenue. Vehicles would access the basement parking garage via the proposed vehicle ramp and new 10-foot curb-cut on Florentine Avenue. 

Consistent with city bicycle parking requirements, the proposed project includes 37 secured class I bicycle parking spaces and six class II bicycle parking spaces on the project’s Mission Street and Florentine Avenue frontages. The existing 12-foot sidewalk on Mission Street and 8-foot sidewalk on Florentine Avenue would be replaced with new sidewalks per DPW requirements. Two existing curb cuts on Mission St would be removed and a new 10-foot curb cut on Florentine Avenue would be constructed to provide garage access. The proposed project also includes a new 30-foot commercial loading zone on Mission Street near the Florentine Avenue intersection. 

Construction of the project would disturb approximately 2,600 square feet of soil and require excavation to a maximum depth of 6 feet below ground surface for construction of the building’s basement level and spread footing foundation. The project would excavate approximately 1,000 cubic yards of soil. Project construction is anticipated to last 18 to 24 months. No pile driving is proposed.

rows.description_planning: The 36,406-square-foot project site is a vacant, irregularly shaped lot in the interior of the block bounded by Guttenberg, Morse, Brunswick and Lowell streets. The proposed project would construct three new two- to three-story (21- to 26-foot-tall) residential buildings totaling 32,214 square feet. The new buildings would include a total of 19 dwelling units with eleven three-bedroom units and eight two-bedroom units. The dwelling units would be accessed from Guttenberg Street by a new 30-foot-wide curb cut leading to a new approximately 267-foot-long, 20-foot-wide private driveway with approximately 5-foot-wide sidewalks on either side. A total of 29 unbundled vehicle parking spots and 19 bicycle parking spaces would be provided in ground-level parking garages in each building. Approximately 8,000 square feet of private open space would also be provided in the form of rear yards. Solar photovoltaic systems would be installed on the roofs of each building. Site grading would involve excavation to depths of three to 6.5 feet below ground surface. Trenching for utilities would involve excavation to a maximum depth of eight feet below ground surface. The proposed project would include approximately 370 cubic yards of soil export and import to construct the project. The project would require planning commission approval of a conditional use authorization for a planned unit development pursuant to planning code sections 303 and 304.

rows.description_planning: The project is located at 20-28 Fountain Street in Noe Valley on an approximate 7,084-square-foot (sf) sloped lot currently improved with a 1,250-sf single family home. The project proposes to merge the existing two lots into one lot. The project would also remodel the existing home, add an accessory dwelling unit, an estimated 220-sf deck, landscaping, two Class 1 bicycle parking spaces and remove an existing extension to a wooden shed. The project also proposes to construct two new two-unit buildings, located closer to the Fountain Street frontage. The proposed building located at 22-24 Fountain Street would be approximately 5,600 sf in size and include three floors of living space over a basement level plus decks on the third floor and the roof. The second proposed building at 26-28 Fountain Street would be approximately 6,000 sf in size and similar in design to the 22-24 Fountain Street proposed building. Open space for the new buildings would be provided through a combination of rear yards and private third floor and roof decks. Each new building would include two on-site vehicular parking spaces and two Class 1 bicycle spaces at the basement level. Two new curb cuts, approximately 10 feet wide, are proposed on Fountain Street for access to each new building’s garage space. The project would add two new street trees along the Fountain Street frontage. The project requires excavation to approximately 33 feet below grade for a proposed elevator pit and removal of 2,300 cubic yards of material for the installation of a combination mat slab and buttressed retaining wall foundation. Construction is anticipated to last approximately 16 months.

A 510 square foot commercial space will be located at the ground floor on the Mission Street frontage, and a residential unit will be located at the rear of the building. rows.description_planning:
3300 Mission Street currently sits vacant after a June 2016 fire that left the structure uninhabitable. On a lot that is approximately 3,072 sq. ft., the three-story building previously allowed commercial space on the first floor and a combination of 24 Single Room Occupancy ("SRO") units and hotel units on the second and third floors. 

The redevelopment of 3300 Mission will transform the property into a six-story, mixed-used building with approximately 21,700 sq. ft. designed for 35 studio dwelling units that are 100% affordable housing, a residential community space, and 776 sq. ft. of commercial/retail space on the first floor. The redevelopment will preserve the existing three-story façade along Mission and 29th Streets and will connect with the new three-story structure above; the remainder of the building is unsalvageable and will be demolished. Each studio unit will be a minimum of 200 sq. ft. and a maximum size of 350 sq. ft. and feature its own private bathroom and kitchen. 

The AMI range will be 30% to 80%, and the project is maximizing the unit yield by adding three stories that respect the existing building and fit with the scale of buildings in surrounding areas. The project is eligible for and will utilize AB2011 streamlined entitlement approvals. It will also utilize the State Density Bonus Law to obtain three additional stories and four waivers.

administration offices for the maintenance staff, a repair shop for maintenance of vehicles and equipment, mowers, golf cart, staff break room and lockers/bathrooms. The Project includes a surface parking lot 
consisting of 23 parking spaces located at the rear of the proposed building.

The Project would include: (1) modification to the blue-top yard at the front of the site; (2) addition of a single-story structure at the front of the existing building, within a portion of the existing blue-top play yard; (3) modification of an existing play area at the southeast corner of the site and within an existing fenced area; (4) modification of an existing central courtyard play area; and (5) modification of a classroom within the existing gymnasium building to create a kitchen area for on-site food preparation. The Project would further increase the maximum allowable student enrollment from 396 to 436. All four existing on-site street vehicular parking spaces will remain, and additional vehicular parking will continue to be provided per private agreement with neighboring property owner on surface parking lot to east. The project proposes 301 cubic yards of excavation with a maximum depth of 5 feet below existing ground surface.

rows.description_planning: Proposed horizontal and vertical addition to an existing two-story, single-family dwelling and the addition of one residential unit per SB-9.

The 34,714-square-foot sloping lot is located in the Diamond Heights/Noe Valley neighborhood, on the block bounded by Diamond Heights Boulevard, Diamond Street, and Gold Mine Drive. The project site, which has frontages along Diamond Heights Boulevard and Diamond Street, is a vacant undeveloped parcel containing 34 trees (none of which is an endangered, rare or threatened tree species) with no existing structures or curb cuts.  The parcel is zoned RM-1, Residential, Mixed District, Low Density and is in a 40-X height and bulk district. 

The project sponsor proposes to subdivide the lot into five lots and construct four 4-bedroom single-family units on four of the lots, seventeen 3-bedroom condominium dwellings and three 2-bedroom condominium dwellings on the fifth lot, for a total of 24 units (approximately 60,000 square feet of residential uses would be provided in total). The structures would terrace up the sloping lot, extending up to 40 feet in height as measured from Diamond Heights Boulevard (per Planning Code Section 260). 

A total of 8 new curb cuts are proposed, with one along Diamond Heights and seven along Diamond. Thirty-two vehicular parking spaces would be provided in garages along Diamond Heights Boulevard and at the ground floor level of the duplex buildings and two single family homes on Diamond Street. The project would also include 48 Class I bicycle parking spaces.

Ten of the 34 trees existing on or adjacent to the site would be preserved (24 of the existing trees would be removed during a period outside the migratory bird nesting season).  In addition, the project would include planting of approximately 25 new street trees along Diamond Street and Diamond Heights Boulevard, as well as planting of approximately 21 additional trees throughout the site. The project also incorporates a publicly accessible stairway connecting Diamond Heights (Diamond Height Boulevard) to Upper Noe Valley (Diamond Street) and a publicly accessible viewing platform accessible from Diamond Heights Boulevard.  

The project would be constructed in three phases, with construction period lasting approximately 32 months; approximately 12,335 cubic yards of materials would be deported from the site during excavation and construction.
